articles.title_orig: Apple Missed a Chance to Be Revolutionary With Touch-Screen Mac
articles.title_zh: Apple Missed a Chance to Be Revolutionary With Touch-Screen Mac
articles.content_orig:
Apple unveils groundbreaking MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display and Touch for the first time on Mac
The world’s best pro laptop now features an industry-leading tandem OLED display, an intuitive Touch experience, blazing-fast M5 Pro and M5 Max performance and AI capabilities, and up to 24 hours of battery life, all in a thinner, lighter design
CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today introduced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display , featuring breakthrough tandem OLED technology that delivers game-changing front-of-screen performance. Available in 14- and 16-inch models, MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display offers a visual experience unlike any other, transforming pro workflows with up to 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness, an industry-leading 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for exceptional detail, a 120Hz variable refresh rate, and a wider color gamut covering both P3 and Adobe RGB for brilliant colors. The new MacBook Pro also introduces intuitive Touch capabilities on the Mac for the first time, opening up a whole new dimension for pros to interact with their content, from manipulating 3D models to playing musical instruments onscreen. The Dynamic Island now comes to Mac, serving as the home for Spotlight, 1 Live Activities, and Siri AI. 2 And with up to 24 hours of battery life in thinner and much lighter 3- and 4-pound designs, MacBook Pro is more portable than ever, empowering pros to take their work wherever inspiration strikes. 3 Featuring M5 Pro and M5 Max, Apple’s most powerful chips ever built for a pro laptop, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and now up to 16TB of blazing-fast storage, the new MacBook Pro delivers speed and capability for the most demanding workflows. An enhanced six-speaker sound system now provides 50 percent deeper bass and remarkable sound clarity for even more immersive audio. And Thunderbolt 5 and a wide array of connectivity, a 12MP Center Stage camera, studio-quality mics, and the power of macOS 27 with Apple Intelligence and Siri AI complete the MacBook Pro experience. 2 It is available to pre-order starting today, October 28, with availability beginning Friday, November 6.
“The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is a monumental step forward for the Mac,” said Johny Srouji, Apple’s chief hardware officer. “PROLED XDR is the world’s best laptop display. It pairs state-of-the-art tandem OLED technology with advanced algorithms in our display engine to deliver the kind of visual fidelity pros have been dreaming of. And with the magic of Touch coming to MacBook Pro, combined with the game-changing performance of M5 Pro and M5 Max, we’ve created a whole new way for pros to interact with their content, taking their workflows to a completely new level. The new MacBook Pro is the result of the deep integration between Apple silicon, hardware, and software, and there’s simply nothing else like it.”
PROLED XDR: The World’s Best Display in a Pro Laptop
The new MacBook Pro debuts the PROLED XDR display, which uses tandem OLED technology and advances it with breakthrough innovations in every layer, advanced algorithms in the display engine, and a state-of-the-art factory calibration process to deliver Extreme Dynamic Range (XDR) and stunning visual fidelity. With exceptional brightness, striking contrast, and vivid true-to-life colors, PROLED XDR offers the ultimate front-of-screen performance, enabling a new level of visual acuity and precision for content creators, photographers, colorists, and designers who need a reference-caliber display on the go.
A Tandem OLED Display Unlike Any Other
PROLED XDR is the world’s best laptop display, delivering true-to-life color and unparalleled brightness and contrast. The PROLED XDR display offers tandem OLED technology unlike any other, with deep innovations in its layers that keep brightness and grayscale uniform across the entire display, while minimizing internal reflections common in traditional OLED designs. It’s all backed by advanced algorithms in the display engine that precisely control each pixel in real time, plus a meticulous manufacturing process and precise calibration of every panel for consistency from display to display.
Breathtaking Brightness and Contrast
PROLED XDR offers up to 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness, allowing specular highlights to shine with stunning intensity. And through optimizations in the tandem OLED panel and custom compensation techniques, combined with precise control of light across the display, the PROLED XDR display achieves an industry-leading 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio, so even the deepest shadows reveal incredible detail, bringing HDR content remarkably close to reality.
An Advanced Display Engine
The display engine precisely controls the color and luminance of every pixel at the sub-millisecond level, compensating for content, pixel use, temperature, and environment all at once to offer exceptional brightness uniformity and grayscale accuracy, even in fast-motion content. It also monitors and adapts each pixel’s usage over time to preserve stunning image quality. And ProMotion technology delivers adaptive refresh rates from as low as 10Hz for better power efficiency and up to 120Hz for fluid responsiveness for content in motion.
The Ultimate Display for Color-Critical Workflows
PROLED XDR offers pros a super-wide color gamut with P3 and now Adobe RGB — critical for workflows in photography and design — along with notably wider coverage in green and cyan ranges. This results in more than 80 percent Rec. 2020 coverage for HDR video editing and color grading. Cutting-edge factory calibration ensures luminance, white point, and color gamut are precisely aligned with standard targets. Both color spaces are accessible within a single default preset, streamlining pro workflows and making it seamless to switch between them. With the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, pros have a portable reference display on the go.
Stunning Clarity in Bright Light
With up to 2000 nits peak SDR brightness, combined with a state-of-the-art antireflective coating, the display is easy to read even in bright lighting conditions. For even greater visibility, the nano-texture option — now precisely etched into the cover glass — further reduces reflections and glare to eliminate distractions while maintaining an excellent viewing experience.
With breakthrough tandem OLED technology, extreme brightness, and extraordinary contrast, along with a super-wide color gamut, PROLED XDR is truly the world’s best laptop display, giving pros an unparalleled visual experience and setting a whole new bar for the industry.
MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content. Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined. Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place. And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users. Graphic designers can now use the entire display as their canvas, no longer constrained by the area of the trackpad when drawing; musicians can play software instruments right onscreen; and app developers can test how Touch performs in their iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the MacBook Pro display. And these new ways to interact with MacBook Pro work in tandem with the keyboard shortcuts and trackpad gestures pros know and love. In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.

articles.title_orig: Ukraine defies Trump to resume attacks on Russian oil refineries
articles.title_zh: Ukraine defies Trump to resume attacks on Russian oil refineries
articles.content_orig:
Kremlin says Kyiv is ‘simply ignoring’ US wishes days before midterm elections after reported strikes on two oil sites
Ukraine has resumed its attacks on Russian oil refineries in defiance of pressure from Donald Trump ahead of the US midterm elections, with a ceasefire in the occupied town of Oleshky due to end late on Sunday.
Russian state media said on Sunday Ukrainian long-range drones had set fire to the Kstovo refinery in Nizhny Novgorod oblast overnight, soon after a major strike against another big refinery in Samara oblast, owned by the Russian state energy giant Rosneft.
The Wall Street Journal had reported that Ukraine had given in to pressure from the White House to stop bombing Russian energy infrastructure.
Ukrainian officials, however, told the Kyiv Independent newspaper that they never agreed to a demand from Jared Kushner, the US president’s son-in-law, to pause refinery strikes for 30 days. The raids on Russia restarted on Friday, Kremlin officials said, complaining that Kyiv was now “simply ignoring” US wishes.
Trump has blamed the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy , for the rise in global fuel prices, and last month lifted US sanctions on Russian diesel.
Zelenskyy has not acknowledged the latest refinery attacks, in an apparent attempt to avoid angry US reprisals. Instead, he said his armed forces had hit a defence industry enterprise in Russia’s Rostov region that made missiles. A Pantsir missile system was destroyed, he said, as part of Ukraine’s ongoing “long-range sanctions”.
Zelenskyy said his country was obliged to retaliate because of a remorseless campaign by Moscow, using drones and ballistic missiles, against vulnerable city-based energy facilities. Four Ukrainian regions were hit by Russia overnight, with electricity cut as a result in hundreds of thousands of households.
“The intensity of the strikes is very high, and the Russians are seeking to maximally exploit the ​deficit of ballistic missile interceptors,” the Ukrainian president said on Telegram. Kyiv experienced power cuts lasting eight to 10 hours on Sunday after a critical thermal power plant was damaged.
Zelenskyy said Russia was suffering record losses, with 54,400 military personnel killed and wounded in October – the highest monthly figure since the full-scale war began. He said Ukraine recaptured 96.2 sqkm (37 sq miles) of its territory last month, 10.4 sqkm (4 sq miles) more than Moscow managed to seize, and emphasised: “Russia is losing.”
The latest attacks came as a six-day local ceasefire brokered by the US first lady, Melania Trump, was due to come to an end in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky. Hundreds of residents were reunited with their loved ones over the weekend in northern Ukraine , with both sides hailing the evacuation mission as a success.
after newsletter promotion
Ukrainian observers say the Russian military used the truce to reinforce its positions and to swap hungry and exhausted troops garrisoned in Oleskhy. The town sits on the left bank of the Dnipro River, to the east, and is opposite the larger city of Kherson, which Ukraine recaptured in autumn 2022. A renewed Russian onslaught is inevitable, the observers believe.
The pope said on Sunday he hoped cooperation between ⁠Russia and Ukraine in implementing the Oleshky ceasefire – the most significant since 2022 – would ⁠pave the ⁠way ​for broader peace efforts.
“I hope that the cooperation between the parties, which made this necessary humanitarian gesture possible, will strengthen their willingness to engage in dialogue,” he said during his Sunday prayer.
Trilateral talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the US are likely to take place later this month, with Kremlin officials saying on Sunday that Vladimir Putin was willing to talk directly with Zelenskyy by phone. They added that European leaders who support Ukraine should not be involved in any such call.
There is little prospect of a wider breakthrough, however, as the Russian president’s maximalist demands remain unchanged. He is insisting that Ukraine give up all of the eastern Donetsk oblast – which Russia has been unable to seize since 2014 – as well as further territory in Kherson and Zaporizhzhia provinces which the Kremlin does not control, but says it has “annexed”.

articles.title_orig: Binance withdrawals resume following $6 billion hack
articles.title_zh: Binance withdrawals resume following $6 billion hack
articles.content_orig:
Cryptocurrency exchange says 90% of losses covered as FBI blames North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor
The cryptocurrency exchange Binance has started to allow its customers to withdraw their funds from the platform, as it recovers from a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack.
The exchange was hit by the theft on Thursday, which has since been described as the biggest heist in history, with experts identifying North Korea as the likely culprit.
Binance initially froze withdrawals as it investigated the breach, but on Sunday announced that it had began a phased reopening after 2pm Singapore time.
In the first phase people holding the ethereum, USDT and USDC tokens on the ethereum blockchain were able to withdraw their funds, as well as some others held on the BNB Smart Chain blockchain. Later on Sunday, dealing in the Dogecoin and Avalanche currencies resumed on their own platforms.
The platform said it had replenished 90% of the ⁠amount stolen. The remaining 10% of tokens were less liquid, meaning they ⁠may take ​longer to buy, the company said in a post on X on Saturday.
Richard Teng, Binance’s co-chief executive, said separately that the company was “committed to covering the ⁠remaining 10%” and users would not bear the financial impact of the hack.
after newsletter promotion
It came as the FBI on Saturday confirmed earlier suspicions from private investigators and analysts that a North Korea-affiliated group called TraderTraitor was behind the hack.
TraderTraitor is believed to be part of the Lazarus Group, which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for The Interview, a film that mocked the North Korean leader Kim Jong-un.
“The Federal Bureau of Investigation is releasing information advising the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6bn in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about October 29,” the law enforcement agency said in a statement.
The FBI added that it had observed “TraderTraitor actors” converting stolen assets into ethereum, and expected those assets to be laundered further by converting them using decentralised finance and instant swap services.
It said it was urging private sector entities “to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors” were “using to launder these stolen assets”.
Teng said on Friday that the breach was a “complex attack” involving a compromised laptop and malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity, making it ‌harder to trace and investigate.
Binance said it had set aside about $6.34bn of company funds to cover the losses. “Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident,” the company said.
The money spent rebuying tokens came from using part of its $1bn secure asset fund for users, a bitcoin reserve it holds to protect customers in the event of security breaches, as well as some ⁠of its futures insurance fund and own corporate treasury, the company said ​on X.
The attack on Binance came as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols.
Bitcoin plunged nearly 5% after the news of the hack, while ethereum dropped nearly 6% and BNB, native to Binance, tumbled nearly 10%.
The sheer scale of the hack has put a spotlight on the capacity of North Korea – which faces extensive international sanctions over its nuclear and missile programmes – to find illicit means to capture revenue.

articles.title_orig: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say
articles.title_zh: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say
articles.content_orig:
Mourners attend the funeral of five Palestinians, who were killed in an Israeli strike
Israeli strikes in Gaza have killed at least eight people, including a child, according to hospitals, despite a year-old ceasefire.
In Gaza City to the north, hospital officials said a missile attack hit a group of civilians next to Cairo School in the Al-Rimal neighbourhood, killing three people, including a four-year-old boy.
In the southern city of Khan Younis, the Hamas-run ministry of interior said a drone attack targeted a group of police officers in the Al-Mawasi area, killing five, as they were carrying out their routine duties.
The Israeli military said it had carried out two attacks on what it described as military operatives but has not yet provided evidence or further information.
Outside Gaza City's Shifa Hospital, video showed a crowd of men gathered to pray next to two body bags and the tiny body of the child, which was wrapped in a white towel.
"My son and his child were martyred. They were sitting in their tent, bothering no one, and nothing else was happening in the area when suddenly, a missile struck them, and they were martyred," Ali Oweis told AFP news agency. "There is no ceasefire; the war is ongoing, don't you see?"
At Nasser hospital in Khan Younis, women despaired as body bags lay on the floor, video showed. The interior ministry named the five police officers killed, who were between the ages of 23 and 53, and called the attack a "horrific massacre".
A ceasefire came into force in Gaza in October last year, but Israeli air strikes have continued almost every day.
Since then, 1,580 people have been killed, according to Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN. Israel says it is targeting Hamas, but often civilians are also killed.
Meanwhile, a peace plan for Gaza, brokered by the Trump administration, has stalled.
The ceasefire saw thousands of Palestinians held by Israel released in return for all of the 48 remaining hostages held in Gaza, and an agreement to end the war.
The conflict was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 taken hostage.
Since the war began, 74,594 people have been killed in Gaza, according to the territory's health ministry.

articles.title_orig: Inside Xiong'an: How China's "City of the Future" Blends Smart Governance with Sustainable Growth
articles.title_zh: Inside Xiong'an: How China's "City of the Future" Blends Smart Governance with Sustainable Growth
articles.content_orig:
Leadership to pursue ‘full and rigorous party self-governance’ with ‘not the slightest hesitation or retreat’, Xi says as fifth plenum ends
Chinese President Xi Jinping has mounted a direct defence of the campaign for strong Communist Party governance and internal discipline, describing them as a “fundamental guarantee” for China’s rise and warning against any easing of scrutiny, according to state media.
Xi took the floor as the party’s 20th Central Committee closed its fifth plenum on Thursday, to directly address the scepticism over the sweeping campaign, state news agency Xinhua reported on Sunday.
According to “side notes” released by Xinhua on a document formally approved at the end of the four-day plenary session, Xi emphasised the need to “further raise awareness of the importance and urgency of relentlessly advancing the party’s full and rigorous self-governance”.

articles.title_orig: India’s Congress Party Holds Mass Protest in New Delhi
articles.title_zh: India’s Congress Party Holds Mass Protest in New Delhi
articles.content_orig:
Tens of thousands of protesters took to the streets of New Delhi on Sunday as India's opposition demanded the resignation of the country's chief election commissioner over a controversial overhaul of voter rolls.
The demonstrators answered a call from the opposition INDIA alliance, led by the Congress party.
Removing Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar would be the "first step towards putting the country back on the right track," opposition leader Rahul Gandhi told the crowd at the main rally
Gandhi accused Kumar of undermining India's electoral process through his actions.
The overhaul of electoral registers, which has seen around 130 million names removed, has sparked weeks of controversy.
Critics accuse the independent Election Commission of making changes that favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Hindu-nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). Both the commission and the BJP reject the allegations.
The commission says the review is intended to remove duplicate entries and the names of deceased people or those no longer eligible to vote.
Previous demonstrations, particularly those led by the youth-driven "Cockroach" movement, have resulted in thousands of arrests in Delhi and other cities.
The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), which describes itself as a "satirical political movement" and organizes supporters largely online, also backed Sunday's opposition protests.
Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda, a senior BJP politician, accused the opposition of engaging in a "deliberate conspiracy" over the latest demonstrations.

articles.title_orig: US photographs China’s secret spaceplane from 56 miles away after years of mysterious missions
articles.title_zh: US photographs China’s secret spaceplane from 56 miles away after years of mysterious missions
articles.content_orig:
The space race is intensifying, and not necessarily because of efforts to explore other worlds. The United States, Russia and China are increasingly competing for influence beyond Earth, with their ambitions extending well beyond scientific research and space exploration.
Several weeks ago, the United States acknowledged that it had deployed a weapon in Earth orbit, prompting swift reactions from its two main geopolitical rivals.
Beijing called on Washington to stop “expanding its military capabilities and preparing for war in outer space,” while Moscow advocated keeping space free of weapons. More recently, reports emerged of an unusual maneuver involving a Russian satellite pursuing an American spacecraft.
Now, another development has highlighted just how intense the competition in orbit has become.
Vantor, a US-based satellite imagery and geospatial intelligence company, has released a photograph of China’s secretive Shenlong spaceplane . Until now, the only publicly available image of the spacecraft had been a blurry photograph in which sunlight reflecting off its panels obscured much of its structure.
The new image was captured from approximately 56 miles (90 kilometers) away in 2024 and was published in recent days as part of a Defense Intelligence Agency report assessing the scale and nature of threats in space.
“Commercial space is now a critical part of the national security toolkit. Commercial imagery and analytics give the US and its allies greater visibility into activity on orbit and help decision-makers understand emerging capabilities,” Vantor explained.
With a resolution of approximately 1.8 inches per pixel, the photograph reveals previously unseen details of the Chinese spacecraft.
The image appears to show Shenlong alongside another satellite, with its panels deployed and its payload bay doors open. The photograph could offer important clues about the activities of the spacecraft, which embarked on its fourth mission in February 2026.
The @DefenseIntel latest Challenges to Security in Space report makes clear that competition in space is accelerating as China and Russia advance their capabilities. The report documents China’s expanding presence in space, including reusable space systems, and features Vantor’s… pic.twitter.com/yHQw1tRZ23
According to China’s space authorities, Shenlong is designed to test technologies that will “pave the way for more convenient and affordable round-trip methods for the peaceful use of space in the future.”
However, independent observers have reported that the spacecraft has released unidentified objects during its missions , raising questions about the precise nature of its activities.
In June 2026, for example, space-monitoring company LeoLabs reported detecting an object near the Chinese spacecraft.
“We have independently cataloged this object and determined with high confidence that it was released from the Chinese spacecraft,” the company said at the time.
Although China’s official explanation emphasizes the development of reusable space transportation technology, the spacecraft’s activities remain largely undisclosed.
The latest photograph offers a rare glimpse of a vehicle that has spent years conducting mysterious missions in orbit, at a time when competition between the world’s major space powers is becoming increasingly difficult to separate from their military and strategic ambitions.

articles.title_orig: Israel’s president says parties need to engage with ‘open heart’ to avoid fresh election
articles.title_zh: Israel’s president says parties need to engage with ‘open heart’ to avoid fresh election
articles.content_orig:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog has urged the country’s political parties to enter negotiations on forming a new government with an “open heart,” as he prepares to consult with factions on a path forward after an uncertain election result.
Last week’s elections saw Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc denied a majority, with the parties in his ruling coalition claiming 53 seats in Israel’s 120-member Knesset.
Parties in the bloc aligned with Netanyahu’s main rival, Gadi Eisenkot , won 48 seats, leaving neither man with an obvious path to forming a government.
The balance of power is held by parties representing Israel’s minority Arab community , which nearly doubled its representation in Israel’s parliament with 19 seats. But both Netanyahu and Eisenkot had ruled out working with them prior to the vote.
Netanyahu has since continued to attack the Arab parties, accusing them of holding stances on Gaza and the West Bank he considers unacceptable. Eisenkot, however, has indicated he is open to working with anyone who agrees to four conditions on Israeli sovereignty and opposition to Hamas, potentially opening a path to a deal that could propel him to power and avoid fresh elections.
While Netanyahu is the leader of the single largest party, it is up to Herzog — largely a ceremonial figure — to decide who has the first shot at forming a government. He will hold initial consultations with party officials on Wednesday, beginning a delicate process that could last weeks.
“I hope the representatives will come with an open mind, and today I add: with an open heart,” Herzog said in a statement Sunday. “Come to listen and to be heard, to share ideas, and to find creative solutions to prevent another round of elections.”
Israel launches strikes on Gaza
Netanyahu, who is set to remain in his post as a caretaker until a new government can be formed, has claimed Arab parties used foreign backing to “steal” the elections, without providing evidence. Israeli intelligence agency Shin Bet has said it is investigating possible foreign interference in the election but that the probe was not intended to “cast aspersions” on any specific group.
Arab party leaders have strongly denied any wrongdoing, while Herzog pushed party leaders to accept the election result.
“During an election campaign, candidates naturally and predictably climb to lofty positions,” Herzog said in his statement. “But the elections are over. The election results are a fact. They are a reality. And now is the time to call on all our leaders to stop climbing and face this reality.”
The four conditions Eisenkot set out for prospective partners include recognizing Israel as a Jewish state, committing to the values of its independence, accepting mandatory military service for all Israeli citizens and recognizing Hamas as a terrorist organization.
“Every Knesset member who is willing to sign on to these principles is a potential partner on the path to establishing a new and better government for Israel,” he said in a statement on Saturday. “The door to the government we will form will be open to every public representative who accepts these principles and is ready to rise to the occasion.”
Netanyahu, meanwhile, said Sunday that it was “forbidden” to form a government with Mansour Abbas, head of Arab-led party Ra’am.
He said on X that Abbas wants to establish a Palestinian state with East Jerusalem as its capital, and evacuate Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories, citing an old Ra’am policy platform.
During the campaign, Netanyahu’s Likud party repeatedly alleged that Eisenkot would usher the Arab parties into power.
In one of several AI-generated videos posted by Netanyahu, Eisenkot was portrayed astride a wooden Trojan horse, with Abbas and left-wing politician Yair Golan inside.
Abbas said Friday that he was coordinating with other Arab leaders on “the prospects for forming a government to replace the one led by Netanyahu.”
Eisenkot’s anti-Netanyahu bloc contains a broad array of ideologies and views on the issue, ranging from Golan, who has publicly advocated for a deal with the Arab parties, to Avigdor Lieberman of the right-wing Yisrael Beiteinu party, who continues to oppose working with them.
With that much friction, a stalemate and more elections remain a real possibility.
Fawaz Gerges, a professor of international relations at the London School of Economics, told NBC News that Israel still appears stuck, adding that Eisenkot’s conditions for the Arab parties are effectively asking them to “forsake their identity.”
“I don’t think we will see the opposition led by Eisenkot forming a government in Israel,” he said. “So what we have now is a deadlock.”
For the major Israeli parties, it is a choice “between Israel as a democratic state or Israel as a Zionist exclusive society,” he said.
But Yossi Mekelberg, a senior consulting fellow with the Middle East and North Africa Program at U.K. think tank Chatham House, sees flexibility that could yield a breakthrough.
Parties “make all these promises before the election, and it is obvious that you break at least some of them after the election,” he said.
Freddie Clayton is a freelance journalist based in London.

articles.title_orig: You Might Be Neglecting The One Thing That Keeps Your PC Healthy
articles.title_zh: You Might Be Neglecting The One Thing That Keeps Your PC Healthy
articles.content_orig:
Download this tool and set it to run regularly.
Most people know a desktop PC needs cleaning now and then. The usual advice is physical: Open the case, clear out the dust, check the fans. We've covered that in our guide to cleaning and organizing your Windows PC . But there's a second chore that gets far less attention: the junk piling up inside Windows itself. Microsoft ships a few tools for it, and we wanted to know how well they work, so we ran a scan-only test of each on the same drive. Nothing was cleaned, and nothing was deleted. What follows is what each tool offered to remove.
We tested three tools on a single 1TB C: drive with only about 4 percent free.
Disk Cleanup is the oldest. Microsoft has shipped it with every version of Windows since Windows 98, and it has barely changed: Pick a drive, wait for a short scan, tick the usual suspects (temporary files, thumbnail caches, the Recycle Bin) and press OK.
Storage Sense lives in Settings > System > Storage . Instead of a one-off scan, it's meant to work in the background, emptying the Recycle Bin, clearing Downloads and removing temporary files on a schedule.
Microsoft PC Manager is a free, separate install that bundles a one-click boost, a storage cleaner and a few extras. Its storage page runs a deeper scan and sorts what it finds into categories.
Disk Cleanup offered to free a meager 1.66GB of junk. Storage Sense offered the exact same 1.66GB, while PC Manager listed 26GB, but that figure includes things that aren't actually junk, such as 15.5GB of items it left unticked, so it overstates the real total.
To see which number to trust, we measured the drive manually and found that it holds roughly 20GB of real junk. Disk Cleanup and Storage Sense found about 8 percent of it, while PC Manager's list covered about 90 percent of the actual junk files. The biggest offenders were a 9.25GB NVIDIA shader cache, about 5GB of Chrome cache across four profiles and 2.2GB of app crash dumps. Both Windows tools missed all of them. PC Manager found them, along with a few caches that developer tools like Python and Node.js leave behind.
There is little reason left to run Disk Cleanup. Microsoft says the tool overlaps in function with Storage Sense, and the test shows why: Storage Sense's "Temporary files" list matched Disk Cleanup's exactly, category for category. Same engine, same cautious rules, and Storage Sense does more on top.
Storage Sense is the better tool, but it's built to work quietly in the background, and on the test drive it did nothing. Windows reported "0 bytes" cleaned in the past month. By default, it only runs when disk space is low, and apparently Windows doesn't count 3.9 percent free as low. Items from six months ago were still sitting in the Recycle Bin.
The fix is a setting. Open Settings > System > Storage > Storage Sense and change Run Storage Sense from During low free disk space to every day, week or month. The Recycle Bin and Downloads thresholds can be set anywhere from 0 to 60 days.
PC Manager was by far the most thorough tool in the test. It preticked 8.9GB as safe to remove, mostly browser caches, crash dumps and temporary files. It left the NVIDIA cache (9GB) and Python (2.7GB) unticked, so the decision on those stays with the user, which is very sensible.
PC Manager also offers a Manage large files option. It lists the biggest files on your drive, so you can decide which are worth keeping and which can go. Nothing is judged for you; the app just shows where the space is going. On our test drive, it found 238GB of files that were bigger than 10MB. It isn't perfect. It nags about "Boost" and health checks, and some of what it frees is cache that will grow back anyway. Still, it's a good option to have.
When most people want to free up space, they open Installed apps , pick the ones they no longer use and hit Uninstall . The catch is that many programs don't leave cleanly. Folders, caches and registry entries often stay behind. Revo Uninstaller Free handles that better: It runs the program's own uninstaller first, then scans for leftover files, folders and registry entries and offers to remove them.
CCleaner used to be the default recommendation, but skip it. It has since turned into bloatware, and its trust problems are on record: In 2018, Avast's Piriform pulled version 5.45 after it was found to be collecting more usage data than users expected.
If you want to maintain a clean computer, you don't need much. Set Storage Sense to run weekly or monthly, and do a PC Manager deep cleanup once a month. When you remove an app, use Revo Uninstaller so nothing is left behind.
Don't expect miracles, though. Removing every byte of junk on our test drive only moved free space from about 4 percent to about 6 or 7 percent. To really clean up space, you'll have to clear out the usual culprits: video games, video files, photo libraries and the like. If your drive is nearly full, use PC Manager's large-file finder to see where it all went, then decide what's worth keeping. Our guide to seeing what's taking up space on your Windows PC walks through the rest.

articles.title_orig: Inside the leaderless movement set to govern Serbia
articles.title_zh: Inside the leaderless movement set to govern Serbia
articles.content_orig:
Aleksandar Vucic is accustomed to the spotlight. As Serbia 's all-powerful president, loyal media outlets followed his every move for years. His TikTok outbursts led the evening news. But on October 25 he lost the election to the Student List, and since then, a lot has changed.
Vucic complained at a press conference, before fewer microphones than usual, that the winners were practising "revolutionary terror." He threatened: "If they continue to terrorize those who think differently – beatings, destruction and all the rest – and the state authorities do nothing, we will be forced to organize ourselves."
Vucic regards the immediate resignation of the general director of the Serbian state broadcaster RTS as an example of this "terror." Senior RTS editors have also been dismissed.
On Monday, a small group of protesters invaded the Informer TV station. Thousands of complaints have been lodged against Informer over the years for its demonization of Vucic critics. Now, journalists' associations are calling for its license to be revoked.
Tabloid media outlets loyal to Vucic have already changed their tone. Unlike Informer, they no longer refer to the Student List as "terrorists" and "mercenaries."
The List, which emerged from the student revolt , is made up of professors, activists and artists. In the election on October 25, it won 53% of the vote , leaving Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) trailing with just 39%.
Since then, things have moved fast. In many cities, citizens peacefully removed portraits of Vucic from municipal buildings. The public prosecutor's office for organized crime has launched investigations, including into electoral fraud. A special commission is examining the work of the Higher Public Prosecutor's Office in Belgrade, which critics say did Vucic's bidding, and persecuted his opponents.
The accusations against him are old ones: that he and his system kept the media under tight control ; that state contracts were only awarded to companies loyal to the regime; and that Vucic, his party, and the Serbian state had links to organized crime .
The catalyst for the revolt was the collapse, two years ago, of the concrete canopy on the newly renovated railway station in Novi Sad. Sixteen people died . The accident is believed to have happened as a result of poor workmanship and corruption in the awarding and execution of the renovation contract.
Those who were celebrating in the streets a few days ago are already growing impatient. The new parliament has not yet been convened, and the SNS still controls many levers of power.
"A society that was oppressed for so long by a party that acted like a feudal lord now, understandably, expects justice," Dejan Bursac from the Institute for Philosophy and Social Theory at Belgrade University told DW. "In this power vacuum, people are getting impatient."
Vucic and leading officials promise to be a strong opposition, and expect to make a quick comeback once "this lot" have ruined the country. But the majority of critics are calling for Vucic to be investigated and charged. "The SNS people are acting as if they had lost a local election somewhere in democratic Scandinavia, not as if they were part of a deeply corrupt and criminal regime," said Bursac.
It's very common in Serbia for politicians to switch allegiance from one camp to another. They go where the power is. Even Vucic has admitted that many of his former comrades-in-arms are turning their backs on him. "We are going to see cases of people resigning or staying in the shadows, even putting themselves forward as informants for the next government," said Zlatko Minic from Transparency Serbia , an organization that monitors the work of governments.
The million-dollar question is: How much damage can the old government do to the new one? "There's still time for many officials to award contracts and create financial obligations for the agencies they run without necessarily committing a criminal offense," Minic warned.
However, those familiar with the situation said that for some time now the Student List has had contacts with officials in the police and administration opposed to Vucic's style of government. The winners of the election may now be able to prevent certain actions. On Wednesday, the List again demanded the resignations of leading officials in the police and judiciary. Whistleblowers were also asked to come forward if the outgoing government should try to "destroy documents."
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
In a symbolic move, Student List representatives held their first press conference in Pioneers Park in front of the parliament building. Vucic's followers fenced off the park in 2025, turning it into a pro-government encampment. According to investigative journalists, it also became a base for thugs and criminals who attacked anti-government demonstrators. The morning after the Student List's election win, its supporters went out with binbags and cleaned up the park.
The victorious Student List unites left- and right-wingers, pro-European and pro-Russian forces. It is focussed on making changes in domestic politics, and wants to advance European Union accession talks by implementing real reforms. The List opposes sanctions on Russia and the recognition of Kosovo — positions that almost the entire population of Serbia agrees with.
"Our plan is to stabilize and develop the country, not to destabilize it with some abrupt change of course on foreign policy," Oliver Toskovic, a psychology professor and future member of parliament, told DW.
Toskovic said that, unlike under Vucic, the EU will not be misused as a "cover." Serbia's EU accession process recently stalled, with Vucic accusing "the West" of inciting a "color revolution" in Serbia.
"We are very dependent on Russia for energy. This is really a mistake of the previous government," Toskovic said. "But for that reason, sanctions right now would destabilize the country. And that would not be good for us or for the EU." How energy policy will develop under a Student List government is still unclear.
Where Vucic would frequently take aim at Kosovo, Croatia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina, leading representatives of the new List have promised better relationships with Serbia's neighbors and a reduction in tensions. On Kosovo, Ilija Srdanovic, the Student List's lead candidate, has said the party is open to dialog with the government in the Kosovar capital, Pristina. He has already spoken by phone with the prime minister of Croatia.
The electoral process is not yet over. On Sunday, November 1, the vote will be repeated in some 50 polling stations because there were irregularities first time around. Once these votes are counted, parliament can be convened. The formation of a government is expected to be quick, but for now the names of the prospective members have not been disclosed.
This article has been translated from German.

articles.title_orig: China’s Communist Party Tightens Internal Discipline, Demands Unwavering Loyalty
articles.title_zh: China’s Communist Party Tightens Internal Discipline, Demands Unwavering Loyalty
articles.content_orig:
China's ruling Communist Party emphasized loyalty in a new resolution aimed at strengthening internal discipline and continuing its anti-corruption efforts.
China’s ruling Communist Party emphasized loyalty in a new resolution aimed at strengthening internal discipline and continuing its anti-corruption efforts. This resolution, discussed at a recent party leadership meeting, calls for enhancing loyalty among members and judging officials based on their commitment to party values, as seen through their work, behavior, and family values.
The resolution acknowledges ongoing problems such as ideological and organizational impurities and aims to address them through an extensive anti-graft campaign that has already affected millions in the bureaucracy. This initiative comes in anticipation of a leadership change where President Xi Jinping is expected to secure another five-year term.
The party plans to improve oversight of officials, including stricter checks on personal disclosures and the financial activities of their families. The anti-corruption campaign will also target hidden forms of graft, including the misuse of technology and financial systems to facilitate corruption.
While promoting collective leadership, the document still reinforces Xi’s authority, urging party members to support him fully in thought and action. Xi emphasized the importance of rigorous self-governance to maintain the party’s integrity and legacy for future generations.

articles.title_orig: Green Party at a "crossroads", says former co-leader Adrian Ramsay
articles.title_zh: Green Party at a "crossroads", says former co-leader Adrian Ramsay
articles.content_orig:
The Green Party is at a "crossroads" and needs to focus on its "core values", a former party co-leader has told the BBC, weeks after members adopted a motion declaring Zionism a form of racism.
Adrian Ramsay suggested the Greens need their policies to appeal to a majority of British voters if they want to bring the "environmental changes that we need" and advised against taking an approach that risks being "quite divisive".
Green Party leader Zack Polanski responded by saying there was "no environmental justice without social, racial and economic justice".
The motion, which Polanski did not take part in or vote upon, defined Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state" that had led to the "disenfranchisement and destruction" of Palestinians.
It backed the creation of a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine", which includes modern-day Israel.
Members of the Green Party of England and Wales adopted the policy motion last month.
It led to a backlash from some Jewish groups, as well as criticism from senior Green figures, including Ramsay and other Green MPs.
Israel's foreign ministry said it had banned Polanski , who is Jewish, from entering the country.
The Equality and Human Rights Commission also wrote to the Green Party asking for more information about the motion after concerns were raised by dozens of Labour and Lib Dem MPs and Jewish campaigners.
Labour later said it would end power-sharing agreements with the Greens on local councils, unless its councillors disowned the policy.
Speaking to Newscast , Ramsay replied "no, it's not" when asked if he thought Zionism is racist before adding he agreed with Polanski and others in believing that what is happening in Gaza is "appalling".
The MP for Waveney Valley, who joined the party in 1998, said he does think Israel has a right to exist, something Polanski has stopped short of saying.
Ramsay also said he has made it clear he is "deeply uncomfortable" with the motion adopted and suggested there is an "opportunity to take some action in relation to the motion in the run-up" to the party's spring conference next year.
He said the question now is how Polanski and the party as a whole responds to the motion.
Ramsay said: "I think there's a real crossroads point for the party at the moment.
"One option is to sort of dig in more down this approach, not only in relation to this motion, but I think that there's a risk it brings with it - a quite divisive, a quite internally focused approach to politics."
Ramsay said this is "perhaps seen from small groups of people on the hard left of politics who go around different parties try to influence how those parties are run".
He added: "What I want to see is the party really focus back in on our core aims as a party and our core values."
Ramsay said this includes ensuring the party is "consensus-building in how we approach our politics" and that "we engage the grassroots of our membership".
He added the party needs to be "very externally focused, because we're only going to be able to bring the environmental changes that we need to have to safeguard our society for now and for the future if the majority of the British public come behind that".
Ramsay served as co-leader of the Greens from 2021 to 2025 alongside Carla Denyer, who is also now an MP.
He unsuccessfully stood on a joint ticket with fellow MP Ellie Chowns in 2025, with the pair losing to Polanski in the leadership contest .
Polanski, who missed the conference vote to unsuccessfully campaign for election in a Westminster by-election, previously said he wants to see the "imperfect" motion amended in future.
However, he said the "substantial part of the motion", that "the displacement and genocide of the Palestinian people is clearly underpinned by a racist ideology" was "obvious". Israel has repeatedly denied its actions in Gaza amount to genocide.
Under Green Party rules, motions supported by members become official party policy, but will not necessarily be included in the party's manifesto at the next general election.

In his Power On newsletter today , Gurman said the next iPad Air will also feature an OLED display, while he expects the next iPad Pro to be equipped with a vapor chamber system that dissipates heat for improved sustained performance. Presumably, the next iPad Air will get an M5 chip, while the iPad Pro will move to the M6 chip.
As for the entry-level iPad 12, previously rumored features for the device include an A19 chip that enables Apple Intelligence support, an N1 chip with Wi-Fi 7 support, and Apple's power-efficient C1X modem in cellular models.

articles.title_zh: Pixel 11 Pro Fold: Sturdy rectangle in a wide wide world
articles.content_orig:
Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now.
Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE.
It’s strange to write this review when the world is focused on the passport-sized iPhone Duo, and China-based companies are busy releasing wide foldables with a similar design. Google, however, stuck to its guns this year and produced a Pixel 11 Pro Fold, which is pretty much similar to last year’s foldable.
The changes involve a lighter design, a brighter display, better wireless charging, and an updated camera sensor. The new olive color looks subtle but gorgeous, so that’s a bonus. However, with all the options out there, the device might not attract people who might be looking to buy their first foldable — unless they’re serious Pixel fans.
Nonetheless, I have enjoyed using the device because the Pixel 11 Pro Fold’s cameras are competent enough, even if they aren’t a match for the Pixel 11 Pro’s setup, and the screen is nice to use despite the very visible crease.
The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is 5mm thick when unfolded (vs 5.2mm of the Pixel 10 Pro Fold) and 10.1mm thick when folded (vs 10.8 mm of the Pixel 10 Pro Fold). This one is for the spec sheet because you might not feel as much difference. Despite this, the phone is not as thin as a device like the Honor V6 Magic.
The difference you might notice — if you hold both this year’s and last year’s foldables — is that the new device is 19 grams lighter. But if you are buying a new device or switching from another foldable, it’s barely noticeable.
The Pixel 10 Pro Fold was already a sturdy device. With this year’s version, the company claims to have increased durability by three times. Plus, there is a new glass-ceramic cover and a glass-fiber composite back cover to take up any impact. My Pixel 10 fell a few times from the table and from my pocket, but there wasn’t any visible dent or scratch. Well done, Google.
One drawback of a strong hinge is that you can’t unfold the 11 Pro Fold with one hand, and that’s by design.
The outer display is ever so slightly bigger, but the more observable change is the 3,600-nit display that is an upgrade from last year’s 3,000-nit peak display. This means that you can use the phone in bright conditions better.
Google’s foldable still has a very visible crease in an age where phone makers like Oppo and Honor have managed to reduce the visibility significantly. The crease is more pronounced in bright light, given there is no reflective display on the device.
On the back, there is the new HiLight indicator, which still lights up only for calls from your favourite contacts, and when you are talking with Gemini hands-free. There isn’t much to talk about this feature beyond that.
Reading and watching videos on a foldable is still fun, though a wide foldable might show an edge on videos. The multitasking is good, but you can only open two apps side by side. Some apps that are tuned for foldable are great to use. For instance, Gmail, being a Google app, lets you see your inbox on one side and a particular email on the other. This can help you get through emails faster. However, Slack doesn’t have this split view, and it’s frustrating because we have been through many cycles of Android foldables with apps still not suited for the expanded screen.
Given how quick Apple developer system moves, Android might feel it’s lagging in foldable experiences after the iPhone Duo is out. The camps are divided as to how apps look on Duo’s unfolded phone, but developers are rapidly updating their apps to fit the unfolded screen.
The bubbles, which let you access apps in floating windows and minimize them in a taskbar, are a good idea. That way, you can temporarily look at information in an app without having to make it a full-sized window.
Gemini updates this year were muted. The company built on its idea of Magic Cue to give timely suggestions in different apps. As I mentioned in my Pixel 11 Pro XL review , Rambler was my favorite feature to use in the new Pixel lineups. I could easily reply to emails and texts, and take notes, without involving texting on a wide keyboard.
Foldables have mostly had inferior cameras to their candybar counterparts for years now. While this year is no different, Google continuing to use the “Pro” moniker for its foldable feels like a disservice. The Pixel 11 Pro Fold cameras are good, but they aren’t Pixel 11 Pro XL good.
There are a few positives with the new version. There is an updated main sensor, still a 48-megapixel one, that lets more light in for photos with better detail. Google has also updated its models to support 30x Super Res Zoom, up from 20x Super Res Zoom.
Even if Google wouldn’t include the same ultrawide and telephoto sensors as the slab Pro devices, I wish they would use the same main sensor on the Fold as the rectangle phone. The telephoto and ultrawide sensors are similar to last year’s device, so there is barely any improvement in images taken from them.
In terms of software features, there is Looks, which can change the tone of an image with different presets, and Magic Capture, which can pick the best frames from a video — useful for when you have pets or kids.
At $1,899, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold is for someone who likes Pixels and wants a foldable, given it’s barely $100 less than the new iPhone Duo and the same price as the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, which are both wide-format phones. In the U.S., the taller Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra starts at $2,099.
In Europe, companies like Xiaomi and Honor are going to release their foldables, too. So Google’s foldable is going to face a lot of competition.

A Qatari tanker has been hit by “unidentified objects” while sailing in the Gulf, the Qatar Gas Transport Company says, the latest attack on commercial shipping since the US-Israel war on Iran began in February.
The attack on Friday evening struck the liquefied natural gas (LNG) carrier Al Mayeda, which belongs to the company, it said in a statement on Sunday.
None of the crew members was injured and no environmental damage was reported, it said.
The statement, published by the Qatar Stock Exchange, said the vessel is currently in a “safe condition, operational” and that the impact of the incident is being assessed.
Qatar expressed “strong condemnation and denunciation of the attack”, its Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement on X.
Doha “considers it a dangerous act that threatens the safety of maritime navigation and the security of global energy supplies”, it said, warning of the regional repercussions of such “reckless and irresponsible practices”.
The ministry said investigations are being conducted to ascertain the circumstances of the incident and identify those responsible, adding that Qatar “reserves its right to take all necessary measures” to protect its property and safeguard its interests.
The Qatar Gas Transport Company supplies Qatari ports and terminals with towage and marine support services.
More than 120 commercial ships have been hit since the start of the war, according to data from the International Maritime Organization and the UK Maritime Trade Operations.
Iran, which closed the Strait of Hormuz early on in the war, has repeatedly warned vessels attempting to pass through the vital waterway without its permission would face “destruction”.
The attacks have increased since the United States reimposed a blockade on Iran’s southern ports in July.
With at least 29 ships hit, October was the worst month of the war, ahead of the 20 attacks recorded in March.

articles.title_orig: At 75, the IRS Will Set the Withdrawal Amount on a $900,000 401(k). Affluent Investors Over 60 Are Making Sure It's Empty by Then - 24/7 Wall St.
articles.title_zh: At 75, the IRS Will Set the Withdrawal Amount on a $900,000 401(k). Affluent Investors Over 60 Are Making Sure It's Empty by Then - 24/7 Wall St.
articles.content_orig:
The IRS gets to decide how much comes out of your 401(k) at 75, and the tax cascade that follows can push your effective marginal rate past 40 percent. There is a narrow window before that clock runs out, and…
The Full Benefits Desk desk. Editor: Gerelyn Terzo .
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
Picture a 62-year-old with $900,000 in a traditional 401(k) and a retirement date coming up soon. He doesn’t want the IRS setting his withdrawals later. If he leaves the account alone, the IRS starts making that call at 75.
Many people are working through the same problem. On Reddit, a 54-year-old with $720,000 in a 401(k) was told, “You’ll probably do a more substantial amount after 65 once you’re on Medicare.” That timing can be expensive.
Under current law, the required minimum distribution (RMD) starting age is 75 for anyone who turns 74 after December 31, 2032. Our 62-year-old was born in 1964, so that rule covers him. If he skips a required withdrawal, he can face a 25% excise tax, falling to 10% if corrected in time.
Roth IRAs get different treatment. The original owner never has to take required minimum distributions while alive. Every dollar that moves to a Roth before 75 is a dollar the IRS can’t force out later.
Assume 5% annual returns and 13 years until age 75. To empty the account by then, he needs to take out about $91,250 at the start of each year.
If he leaves it untouched, the same $900,000 grows to roughly $1.7 million by 75.
The IRS Uniform Lifetime Table divisor at that age is 24.6, so his first RMD comes to about $69,000.
By 85 the divisor drops to 16.0, which increases the required share of the balance from about 4% to over 6% a year.
Say he files jointly and the withdrawal is the couple’s only taxable income early in retirement. The 2026 standard deduction of $32,200 leaves $59,050 of taxable income.
All of it lands in the 10% and 12% brackets, and the 12% bracket runs up to $100,800.
The federal bill is about $6,590, an effective rate near 7%. Whatever part he doesn’t need to live on can instead move directly into a Roth IRA through a taxable rollover. Emptying the pretax account and spending the money are two separate decisions. That converted money can keep growing, with qualified withdrawals tax-free.
Now picture the untouched account at 75, with RMDs stacked on top of Social Security. On a joint return, benefits start becoming taxable once combined income passes $32,000, and the second threshold is $44,000. Up to 85% of benefits can end up taxable.
In that phase-in range, each extra RMD dollar taxed at 22% draws 85 cents of benefits into taxable income along with it. That works out to an effective marginal rate of about 41%.
After the year one spouse dies, the survivor generally files single. Under 2026 rules, the first Medicare surcharge threshold falls from $218,000 to $109,000.
Medicare’s income-related monthly adjustment amount (IRMAA) generally uses income from two years earlier. A conversion at 62 ordinarily won’t affect his Medicare premiums at 65. From 63 on, conversions can affect future premiums. That makes 62 an attractive window, although health insurance costs before Medicare matter too.
Under 2026 rules, a $91,250 conversion alone sits below the joint threshold of $218,000. Add a large capital gain on top and the couple could cross it.
The first level adds $81.20 a month per person to the standard $202.90 Part B premium , plus $14.50 for Part D.
For a married couple who can convert at around 7% now instead of facing a possible 41% marginal rate later, emptying the 401(k) on their own schedule comes out ahead.

articles.title_orig: Israel election: When will government be formed, who will lead it?
articles.title_zh: Israel election: When will government be formed, who will lead it?
articles.content_orig:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has lost his coalition’s parliamentary majority following legislative elections on October 27.
But a bloc of Jewish parties opposing Netanyahu also failed to win a majority in the 120-seat Knesset, leaving Israel without a clear path to a new government.
What’s ahead is likely weeks of political wrangling as Israel’s disparate factions weigh possible governing arrangements, including a unity government bringing rival factions together or a minority government reliant on outside support. If they fail to reach an agreement, Israel could head back to the polls.
Here’s what you should know:
The pro-Netanyahu coalition won 53 seats:
A bloc of Jewish parties opposing Netanyahu won 48 seats:
Arab-led parties won 19 seats:
That leaves all existing blocs short of the 61 seats needed for a majority in the Knesset, meaning some parties would have to realign or join forces across bloc lines to form a new government.
Israel’s election results must be officially certified and presented to President Isaac Herzog by November 4 .
The new Knesset is scheduled to be sworn in on November 10 .
Herzog must task one incoming Knesset member with forming a new government by November 11 . He is expected to make his decision with input from party leaders, selecting the candidate he believes has the best chance of building a coalition.
The candidate commissioned by Herzog has 28 days to form a coalition, with a possible extension of 14 days .
He has not said yet, but the most likely candidates are Netanyahu or former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, whose Yashar party received the most votes in the opposition bloc.
According to Israel’s Yedioth Ahronoth media, Eisenkot may have an edge over Netanyahu as some Arab-led parties consider endorsing him in a bid to oust Netanyahu.
Herzog, for his part, has urged Israeli politicians to move away from rigid partisan stances and look for “creative solutions” that will lead to a new government and avoid a second round of elections.
Before the election, Herzog said he would do everything he could to spare the country another election cycle, even if that means pressing for a national unity government that brings together rivals Netanyahu and Eisenkot.
Eisenkot and other opposition leaders have previously ruled out partnering with the Arab-led parties .
Former Prime Minister Ehud Barak, however, has said he believes they “can change their mind”, arguing that Netanyahu would do in their position.
“If Netanyahu had a similar problem, he would immediately invite Mansour Abbas”, the leader of Ra’am and “give him the role of a minister of interior”, Barak told France 24 on Friday.
Abbas himself has signalled a willingness to work the opposition camp, saying Eisenkot’s conditions would not pose an obstacle for his party, according to Israel’s Channel 12.
Yousef Jabareen from the Arab-led Joint List has also said that his party is ready for the “ousting of the Netanyahu government”.
“The change comes through Jewish-Arab partnership, a true and equal partnership,” he wrote on X.
Even if Arab-led parties do not formally join the opposition’s coalition, they could prop it up from outside by helping it pass a confidence vote in the Knesset.
Raluca Ganea, co-founder of Israeli civil society group Zazim, told Al Jazeera that a coalition between the opposition bloc and the Arab-led parties representing the Palestinian citizens of Israel “is the only path forward for Israeli democracy as a whole”.
If Herzog’s first candidate fails to form a government within the 42 days, the Israeli president has the option of asking another Knesset member to try to do so within 28 days. If that candidate also fails, a majority of Knesset members could put forward a third candidate, who would have a final 14 days to try to assemble one.
Even without a coalition commanding at least 61 seats, a candidate could still try to form a minority government by relying on outside support from smaller parties, including Arab-led parties, or negotiate a power-sharing arrangement with alternating prime ministers.
If none of these options succeed and deadlock persists, the Knesset would be formally dissolved, and Israelis would return to the polls for another round of elections.
Those elections would have to be called within 90 days.
Netanyahu stays on as caretaker prime minister until a new government is formed.
If the process drags out, that could leave Israel’s longest-serving prime minister in power for months more, even if he ultimately fails to become part of the next governing coalition.

articles.title_orig: King to address slavery in Antigua as PM says he is open to possible UK apology
articles.title_zh: King to address slavery in Antigua as PM says he is open to possible UK apology
articles.content_orig:
King Charles III is to speak with "unflinching honesty" and "sincere sorrow" on the lasting pain of the transatlantic slave trade, during the final leg of his Caribbean tour in Antigua, Buckingham Palace has said.
The King will address Commonwealth leaders on Tuesday in a speech which will touch on the issue.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said earlier he was "open" to the possibility of the UK formally apologising for its role in slavery - a change in the government's stance.
It is understood the Palace was told in advance of Burnham's comments in an opinion piece on Friday night, and the King has not made any changes to his speech in light of them.
The British government has never formally apologised for slavery or offered to pay reparations.
Burnham has previously stuck with the policy of his predecessors, and stopped short of offering any consideration of reparation payments.
Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch described "endless talk about apologies" as a "distraction" from solving current problems.
She told BBC Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg: "The transatlantic slave trade happened centuries ago. It is time for the Commonwealth to start looking forwards, not endlessly backwards."
The King will make his speech at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM).
He "will not shy away from confronting the most shameful aspects of the past during this visit", a Palace spokesperson said.
"You may therefore expect him to address them in his speech with unflinching honesty, sincere sorrow, and respect for the wider discussions that will be taking place between relevant governments on this issue at CHOGM and beyond."
When asked about the King's reaction to the prime minister's comments, the spokesperson said it would "not be appropriate" for the King to address matters of policy relating to "the UK government's position".
The Caribbean tour has again thrust King Charles into the difficult debates over the UK's colonial legacy in the region.
On his first stop in the Bahamas, the King delivered a speech where he spoke of the "suffering of the past".
In Guyana, he visited the site of a Slave Rebellion where hundreds of enslaved people were killed.
Buckingham Palace said it was a moment for the King to learn more about the history of slavery and resistance. His engagements have also covered the environment, opportunities for young people and trade relationships with the UK.
Royal sources have stressed that the decisions around making an apology are a matter for government, not the Palace.
"His Majesty is well practised on the diplomatic tightrope," a Royal aide said. "He is up for challenging visits with complex issues and relationships in play. He sees it as his role to 'bat for Britain', the Realms and wider Commonwealth."
In a piece for the Guardian published on Friday night, Burnham described the transatlantic slave trade as a "brutal and barbaric violation" , and that Britain "must face up to the past".
His pledge to strengthen the work of the Commonwealth as an organisation will be welcomed by King Charles, who views the collection of 56 countries as a powerful vehicle for change.
"Institutions are under strain across the globe," said a Palace spokesperson. "The Commonwealth has scale and breadth, but is also small enough for leaders to know each other and co-operate together."
The King, they said, "contributes ideas and encouragement on a wide range of issues, delivering practical results which help improve the lives of millions".
Queen Camilla is with the King in Antigua, they have attended a church service on Sunday morning ahead of joining celebrations to mark Independence Day on the island.
It has been a difficult few months for the King, with developments surrounding his brother, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor , and the publication of a book by his former brother-in-law, Earl Spencer.
In addition, his son the Duke of Sussex made a surprise move back to the UK with his wife Meghan and their two children in August.
Asked if the King was confident that his approach to family matters had been the right one in terms of public attitudes towards the institution, the response was concise. "Yes," a senior aide told the BBC. "That is why he takes the actions he does - and has done."
On the serious allegations that have emerged about Meghan's father , Thomas Markle, the Palace did not want to get involved publicly: "We wouldn't comment on private family matters."
The King is also still being treated for cancer. He was diagnosed in early 2024 and the Palace says he remains on a "positive trajectory".
In hot and humid conditions, he will soon celebrate his 78th birthday and will have carried out about 36 engagements by the end of this nine-day tour of the Caribbean.

The holiday season is hurtling toward us like a freight train, and there's nothing we can do about it — except maybe allow ourselves some retail therapy at Costco, the store that has it all (and in bulk quantities). The wholesale retailer has lots of great new finds for November, so we're highlighting some highly rated items. This month, you'll find cookware, gourmet chocolates, energy drinks, holiday glassware, snacks, and more.
Something to keep in mind about Costco: The store's online inventory and in-store stock aren't always the same. As such, some of these November finds are only available for purchase online. But don't worry — we included links to each product.
You may also notice that our selection is mostly name-brand products, with just one Kirkland Signature item in the mix. While Costco's store brand is beloved for its quality and affordability, the chain stocks a wide selection of name-brand items to ensure members have lots to choose from. Speaking of impressive Kirkland Signature products, here's how Costco's pumpkin pie compares to the one from Sam's Club in terms of tastiness and overall value (after all, it's never too early to start planning your Thanksgiving menu).
This versatile, induction-compatible cookware is great for braising, searing, roasting, and baking. As one Costco member put it in their review, "This braising pan is high quality and even better than I expected. It's my go to pan already for dinner."
You can buy this Tramontina 4-Quart Enameled Cast Iron Covered Braiser online for $58.99.
This gourmet shortbread set comes with 24 individual boxes, which equals 96 cookies in total. That makes them perfect for random gift giving. "I'm going to give out [these cookies] during the holidays to neighbors etc.," wrote a reviewer on the Costco site.
You can buy Mary Macleod's Shortbread Christmas Tree Box of The Classic Shortbread online for $89.99.
If you love crispy snacks but are burned out on chips and pretzels, rice crackers are the next logical step. Dubbed "Best snack crackers ever" by a Costco reviewer, the shopper described them as "Spicy, salty sweet and crunchy you can't do much better." Each 2-pound bag comes with varieties like Chili Mochi, Sesame Half Moon, Wasabi Crescent, and plenty more.
You can buy these Kirkland Signature Rice Crackers online for $12.49.
If you know any chocolate snobs who hold the European view that Hershey's is gross (thanks to one infamous flavor note), Costco has the perfect gift. This 2-pound pack comes with 100 individual pieces in milk, white, and dark chocolate.
You can buy this Hebert Candies Heritage Chocolate Assortment online for $59.99.
This mushroom-infused coffee is a good example of at least one of the food trends that swept through 2026 . Featuring a blend of mushrooms intended to support immune function, reduce stress, and improve concentration, the convenient brew received accolades from Costco reviewers, with one writing, "Portable, delicious and good for you and your brain!"
You can buy 60 servings of Wunderground Craft Instant Coffee Plus Mushroom online for $59.99.
"Very worth the price," wrote a Costco shopper about this cute holiday glassware set. You get four glasses with different seasonally inspired designs. They're also very sturdily made; as another reviewer noted, "The design does not sit on the glass but also feels like a small glass object embossed in the glass."
You can buy this four-piece Pandex Holiday Icon Glasses Set online for $29.99.
According to a review on the Costco website, this holiday-inspired soda is "Really good and taste[s] like a frosted cranberry." Along with seasonal varieties, the soda brand offers lots of regular flavors as well. Here's our ranking of every Poppi flavor from worst to best to whet your whistle.
You can buy an 18-pack of Poppi Soda Cranberry Fizz online for $18.99 (price valid through November 15).
Of all the popular ways to pop popcorn , a stovetop popper offers a one-way ticket to nostalgia town. (Did we mention that it's also among the tastiest methods?) With a 4.4-star member rating as of this writing, this GreenPan popper is currently $12 off its regular price and is compatible with gas, electric, and induction cooktops.
You can buy this GreenPan 5.39 qt. Stainless Steel Popcorn Popper online for $45.99 (price valid through November 22).
Here's the awesome thing about gift bundles like this one from Ethel M Chocolates: There's nothing stopping you from keeping one box for yourself and enjoying rich, decadent flavors like Maple Walnut Satin Crème and Macadamia Salute. "Delish," wrote a Costco reviewer of these gourmet chocolates.
You can buy this Ethel M Chocolates Nuts and Caramels Collection Bundle online for $59.99.
While it doesn't rank among the best-selling energy drinks in the U.S. , Ghost is pretty popular in its own right. In the words of one Costco shopper, "Best energy drinks out there. I don't experience any crash, the flavors are phenomenal, and you can't beat the price!!!" This vibe-licious variety pack includes 18 total beverages and comes in Welch's Grape-Cran, Blue Raspberry, and Strawbango flavors.
You can buy this Ghost Energy Drink Variety Pack online for $32.99.
