articles.title_zh: Roundup: October 2026 deliveries by major Chinese automakers
articles.content_orig:
Deliveries among China's major automakers and EV startups diverged further in October, with Xpeng (NYSE: XPEV) setting a monthly record while Nio Inc (NYSE: NIO) and Li Auto (NASDAQ: LI) posted both year-on-year and month-on-month declines.
According to figures released by the companies on Sunday, Xpeng's monthly deliveries exceeded 50,000 for the first time, with overseas deliveries reaching a record high. Nio's deliveries fell to their lowest level since April, while Li Auto's dropped to their lowest since February.
Leapmotor (HKEX: 9863) delivered more than 100,000 vehicles for the fourth consecutive month, setting another record. Xiaomi Auto delivered more than 50,000 vehicles, its highest monthly total this year.
Deliveries at the Huawei-led HIMA (Harmony Intelligent Mobility Alliance) fell more than 50% year-on-year, pushing its year-to-date delivery growth into negative territory for the first time this year.
Below are the October figures announced by major automakers and brands, with year-on-year, month-on-month and cumulative comparisons based on data compiled by CnEVPost.
BYD (HKEX: 1211) sold 490,168 NEVs in October, up 10.97% year-on-year and 5.74% from September, marking its highest monthly total of the year. This was its sixth consecutive month of year-on-year growth and its eighth consecutive monthly increase.
Battery electric passenger vehicle sales reached 305,743 units, up 37.38% year-on-year, topping 300,000 for the first time and setting a record for the third consecutive month. Plug-in hybrid passenger vehicle sales totaled 177,382 units, down 17.23% year-on-year, marking a second consecutive month of decline.
BYD exported 170,194 NEVs in October, up 102.84% year-on-year but down 5.81% from September. Sales in China totaled 319,974 units, down 10.57% year-on-year but up 13.12% from September.
In the first 10 months of this year, BYD sold 3,621,744 NEVs, down 2.16% year-on-year, narrowing the decline from 3.94% in the first 9 months. Exports rose 93.75% to 1,513,154 units, while domestic sales fell 27.81% to 2,108,590 units.
Geely Auto (HKEX: 0175) sold 310,183 vehicles in October, up 0.99% year-on-year and 6.17% from September, setting a new high for the year for the third consecutive month. It was the company's second-highest monthly total, just 245 vehicles short of the record set last November.
NEV sales rose 20.86% year-on-year to 214,996 vehicles in October, exceeding 200,000 for the first time and accounting for a record 69% of total sales. BEV sales rose 43% to 140,758 vehicles, while PHEV sales fell 6.66% to 74,238.
Exports remained strong at 107,153 vehicles in October, up 157.78% year-on-year and 0.44% from September. Sales in China totaled 203,030 vehicles, down 23.55% year-on-year, a steeper decline than in September, though up 9.46% month-on-month.
By brand, Galaxy sold a record 153,385 vehicles in October, exceeding 150,000 for the first time. Zeekr sold 32,483 vehicles, up 51.63% year-on-year but down 12.72% from September. Lynk & Co sold 21,958 vehicles, down 45.40% year-on-year, marking its seventh consecutive month of decline.
Chery Group sold 295,934 vehicles in October, up 5.25% year-on-year. Sales in the first 10 months of the year totaled 2,502,723 vehicles, up 9.34% year-on-year.
October new energy vehicle (NEV) sales reached a record 140,893, up 27.7% year-on-year and exceeding 100,000 for the seventh consecutive month.
Chery Group exported 200,618 vehicles in October, up 58.67% year-on-year, exceeding 200,000 for the third time this year and accounting for about 68% of its total monthly sales. Exports in the first 10 months totaled 1,751,766 vehicles, up 64.8% year-on-year.
On a separate reporting basis from the group, Hong Kong-listed Chery (HKEX: 9973) sold a combined 282,458 vehicles across its 5 brands in October, up 7.21% year-on-year and 1.99% month-on-month, marking its highest monthly total this year. That included 132,023 NEVs, up 28.17% year-on-year and accounting for 46.74% of its total sales.
GWM sold 120,374 vehicles in October, down 15.87% year-on-year, marking a third consecutive monthly decline and the steepest drop this year. Sales rose 4.72% month-on-month.
Domestic sales in China fell 33.06% year-on-year to 57,512 vehicles, declining for a twelfth consecutive month. Overseas sales reached a record 62,862 vehicles, although year-on-year growth slowed to 9.98%.
NEV sales rose 7.25% year-on-year to a record 49,499 vehicles. NEVs accounted for 41.12% of total sales, exceeding 40% for the first time.
By brand, Haval sales fell 19.50% year-on-year, while Tank and Wey each posted declines of more than 30%. Ora sales rose 115.78% to 12,187 vehicles, the highest since March 2022.
In the first 10 months of the year, GWM sold 1,040,676 vehicles, down 2.42% year-on-year. Overseas sales rose 37.69% to 538,839 vehicles, already exceeding the total for all of 2025.
Nio Inc delivered 34,246 vehicles in October, down 15.23% year-on-year and 8.45% month-on-month, ending 31 consecutive months of year-on-year growth.
This marked the company's first year-on-year decline in monthly deliveries since February 2024 and its lowest monthly total since April this year.
The Nio main brand delivered 18,125 vehicles in October, up 5.73% year-on-year but down 14.98% month-on-month. Onvo delivered 8,383 vehicles, down 51.66% year-on-year and 4.34% month-on-month.
Firefly delivered 7,738 vehicles, up 30.89% year-on-year and 5.61% month-on-month, setting a record for the second consecutive month. It was also the company's only brand to post a month-on-month increase.
In the first 10 months of the year, Nio Inc delivered 334,547 vehicles, up 38.46% year-on-year and already exceeding its full-year 2025 total. However, growth slowed from 49.24% in the first 9 months.
The Nio main brand accounted for 200,113 deliveries, Onvo for 78,574 and Firefly for 55,860. Onvo's cumulative deliveries fell 9.54% year-on-year, reversing growth in the first 9 months.
Xpeng delivered 50,237 vehicles in October, up 19.57% year-on-year and 21.77% month-on-month, surpassing its previous record of 42,013 set in October last year.
Overseas operations provided significant support for growth. The company delivered a record 13,326 vehicles overseas in October, up 166% year-on-year and accounting for 26.53% of total deliveries.
Xpeng delivered 36,911 vehicles in China in October, its highest domestic total in a year, according to CnEVPost calculations.
In the first 10 months, Xpeng delivered 334,604 vehicles, down 5.80% year-on-year, narrowing the decline from 9.20% in the first 9 months. Overseas deliveries totaled 72,805 during the same period.
Chairman and CEO He Xiaopeng previously said the company would aim to exceed 60,000 monthly sales in the fourth quarter.
Li Auto delivered 29,025 vehicles in October, down 8.63% year-on-year and 8.78% month-on-month. This marked its second consecutive year-on-year decline and its lowest monthly total since February.
In the first 10 months, Li Auto delivered 322,461 vehicles, down 1.96% year-on-year, widening the decline from 1.25% in the first 9 months.
The company said deliveries of the new Li Mega exceeded 3,000 in October. A new generation of the flagship battery-electric MPV (multi-purpose vehicle) was launched in September.
The 2026 Li i6 was launched on October 28, with deliveries starting the following day. The updated model features upgrades to its in-house developed driver-assistance chip, battery and cabin features.
Li Auto plans to increase the Li i6's monthly production capacity to 20,000 vehicles in November, with a further increase in December. The delivery ramp-up of the updated model will be a key factor to watch in its upcoming sales performance.
Leapmotor delivered a record 106,127 vehicles globally in October, up 50.99% year-on-year and 0.45% month-on-month, exceeding 100,000 for the fourth consecutive month.

articles.title_orig: Samsung joins cuff-shaped earbuds trend with $229 Galaxy Buds On
articles.title_zh: Samsung joins cuff-shaped earbuds trend with $229 Galaxy Buds On
articles.content_orig:
It's got a clip-on design to keep them in place.
As competitors like Sony, Bose and Sennheiser reveal their takes on open-ear wireless earbuds, Samsung is taking another stab with the Galaxy Buds On, featuring a clip-on design for a more secure fit. While they don't pack high-level noise cancellation like the Galaxy Buds 4 Pro, the company claims its new Audio Leakage Reduction tech reduces sound leakage by protecting reversed sound waves at the rear of each bud, ostensibly canceling it out. The company says it pulled data from over 119 million ear scans to help the Buds On fit across a range of ear shapes and sizes and have IP54 water resistance.
They're also designed to ensure a low-pressure fit around the ear, something many of us crave from open-ear buds, avoiding the discomfort from typical wireless headphones that form a seal around the ear canal. As mentioned, these aren't Samsung's first open-type design; you might recall the underwhelming Galaxy Buds Live . The more recent (and better) Galaxy Buds 4 launched earlier this year and also have an open-type, semi-in-ear profile like recent AirPods.
The Galaxy Buds On pack a new high-efficiency Class-D amplifier designed to balance power consumption and punchy sound. Battery life also looks solid, with an estimated 9.5 hours of music playback on a single charge. With the charging case, that should stretch to 38 hours.
Samsung's newest buds pack three mics and a voice pickup unit (VPU) that detects speech vibrations, which work together to isolate the caller's voice and cut out noise. Algorithms have been trained on a range of ambient sounds, including construction noises and car horns (is that a regular occurrence on your calls?). The Buds On also pack in head-gesture controls: nod or shake your head to accept or decline calls, and even dismiss alarms and notification readouts. The buds will also work with Galaxy smartphone features, including access to Gemini Live, Quick Voice Memo recordings and will connect to Galaxy phones as soon as you open the case.
The Galaxy Buds On will launch in early November 2026 and will be priced at $229.

articles.title_orig: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy
articles.title_zh: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy
articles.content_orig:
More than 300 people have been arrested during a protest supporting the banned Palestine Action group outside the US embassy, police have said.
Hundreds of people gathered at Nine Elms in London on Saturday, with many holding signs reading phrases such as: "I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action."
The Metropolitan Police said on Sunday that 325 arrests were made. The force added on social media that 320 of them were for "expressing support for a proscribed organisation under the Terrorism Act".
At least 4,000 arrests have been made in relation to the group, which was proscribed in July 2025.
The UK Supreme Court is due to review Palestine Action's ban under terrorism legislation , after the group's co-founder was granted permission to appeal it.
The Home Office has said that it will robustly defend against the appeal.
Officers on Saturday made arrests into the evening, taking people to police vans for transfer, to the applause of many protesters, some of whom chanted: "Free, free Palestine."
In some instances, officers had to carry demonstrators who refused to walk.
Retired lawyer Charles Allison - who was taken by police in the afternoon  - had travelled from Cumbria to participate. He said he feared for people's civil liberties, which he said were "being devalued and watered down".
"I hope the Supreme Court justices - they won't necessarily be influenced by it [the protest] - but I hope that they will take a long-term view of what is happening in this country and decide that the proscription was unlawful, as I believe it was," the 75-year-old said.
David Bolden, another protester awaiting arrest called the ban an "absurd law".
Defend Our Juries, which has been co-ordinating a series of protests over the ban, said the number of people detained this weekend took the total over 4,000 arrests since the group was proscribed, calling it "truly dystopian".
According to Home Office figures seen by the BBC, 3,630 arrests were made in the year ending June 2026. Along with the 134 people arrested outside Westminster Magistrates Court earlier this year and those on Saturday brings the total up to 4,089.
The BBC has contacted the Met to confirm any figures it might hold.
Amnesty International UK has criticised the arrests and called for the government to drop the proscription of Palestine Action.
Defend Our Juries called the arrests "unjust" and an assault on free speech.

articles.title_orig: Ukraine Liberated 96 Sq Km in October, Inflicted Record Losses
articles.title_zh: Ukraine Liberated 96 Sq Km in October, Inflicted Record Losses
articles.content_orig:
In brief: Ukrainian Defense Forces liberated 96.2 square kilometers of sovereign territory in October – surpassing Russian territorial advances by 10.4 square kilometers – while inflicting a record 54,400 casualties on the Russian military, President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Sunday, Nov. 1. Calling the milestone the highest monthly toll of the full-scale war, Zelensky noted that Russian daily casualties peaked at 2,250 on Oct. 21. The president also commended all combat units for holding lines, recovering land, and maximizing the war’s cost to the aggressor, emphasizing that Moscow need only choose an immediate ceasefire and diplomacy to halt its losses.
The Defense Forces of Ukraine liberated 96.2 square kilometers of sovereign territory in October – surpassing Russian territorial advances by 10.4 square kilometers – while inflicting an unprecedented 54,400 casualties on the Russian military, President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Sunday, Nov. 1.
Writing on Telegram , the head of state presented a monthly assessment establishing that Ukrainian forces recaptured more land than Russian occupying units seized over the same 31-day period, while extracting the highest monthly casualty toll recorded since the beginning of the full-scale invasion in February 2022 .
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“In October, our Defense Forces of Ukraine inflicted record losses on the enemy and regained more territory than the Russian occupiers were able to capture,” Zelensky stated.
According to data presented by the president, Russian forces suffered 54,400 military personnel killed and severely wounded during the month. The monthly attrition rate also produced a single-day casualty record on Oct. 21, when Russian forces sustained 2,250 casualties within a single 24-hour cycle.
“It is important that we continue to take back what is ours,” Zelensky emphasized.
“During October, the Defense Forces liberated 96.2 square kilometers of Ukrainian land, which is 10.4 square kilometers more than the occupiers managed to capture during this time.”
The president extended formal commendations to all Ukrainian soldiers, combat brigades, and specialized service branches contributing to the counter-offensive maneuvers and frontline containment operations.
“Russia is losing. We are holding positions, liberating territory, and ensuring that every day of the war costs the aggressor as dearly as possible,” Zelensky underscored, adding that to halt these severe losses, Moscow need only choose an immediate ceasefire and genuine diplomacy.
A decisive component of Ukraine’s battlefield efficiency in October stemmed from the operational scale of the Unmanned Systems Forces (USF).
Earlier on Sunday, USF Commander Robert “Madyar” Brovdi reported that drone detachments under his command accounted for 16,796 Russian military casualties in October – nearly 31 percent of the total 54,400 personnel losses confirmed by the president .
Over the course of the month, USF units struck 64,807 adversary targets across 255,605 combat missions, neutralizing a Russian serviceman every 159 seconds on average.
Roughly 69.5 percent of drone-inflicted Russian casualties occurred along the Dobropillia-Pokrovsk, Oleksandrivka, and Huliaipole operational axes, where loitering munitions, thermal-equipped bomber drones, and first-person view (FPV) strike craft disrupted enemy staging areas and armored columns before assault teams reached forward contact lines.
The record monthly losses in personnel and equipment compound cumulative assessments tracking the exhaustion of Russia’s conventional force generation.
A statistical study by The Economist calculated that total Russian casualties since February 2022 range between 1.4 million and 2.1 million killed and wounded , with battlefield fatalities reaching between 374,000 and 770,000.
The publication noted that the sharp escalation in fatal casualties over recent months reflects the increasing reliance of Russian field commands on frontal infantry charges to compensate for armor shortfalls.
The mounting losses have severely strained Russian domestic labor reserves, prompting Moscow to deploy thousands of North Korean troops in frontline combat while utilizing illicit overseas networks to bring North Korean forced laborers into Russian defense factories on fraudulent student visas, according to recent human rights investigations by Global Rights Compliance.
Concurrently, Ukrainian forces have coupled frontline resistance with precision interdiction against Russian military-industrial supply chains and energy hubs.
Over the final days of October, Ukrainian precision strikes destroyed an S-400 Triumf command post and a Pantsir-S2 complex valued at $70 million alongside the Kamensky solid rocket fuel plant in Rostov region, while long-range drones struck major oil processing refineries in Kstovo, Ufa, and Novokuybyshevsk.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

articles.title_orig: Poland’s fight over its constitutional court gets physical
articles.title_zh: Poland’s fight over its constitutional court gets physical
articles.content_orig:
Poland is in the throes of a constitutional crisis as a battle over the future of the country’s highest court ignites another confrontation between the country’s president and prime minister.
The crisis came to a head on Friday when center-left Prime Minister Donald Tusk moved to remake Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal, whose chief justice was appointed by the previous government – the far-right Law and Justice party (PiS).
The judge, Bogdan Święczkowski, was suspended after refusing to allow a new member of the Tribunal, who had been nominated by Tusk and approved by the Polish parliament, from taking his seat. His deputy was also suspended.
The current crisis is the latest and possibly most serious chapter in a long-running dispute over the rule of law in Poland.
Tusk’s pro-European Civic Coalition was elected in 2023, after an election campaign in which he promised to restore the Tribunal’s independence. President Karol Nawrocki, who belongs to PiS, was elected separately last year. Poland’s president has little executive power but plays an important constitutional role.
Since then, deadlock has become crisis.
Nawrocki described Święczkowski’s removal as the chief judge as “a forcible takeover of a constitutional body.” On hearing the news, he abandoned a trip to Africa, ordered his aircraft to turn round and headed straight to the Tribunal.
Nawrocki is a vocal supporter of US President Donald Trump, who said in September: “I endorsed him, and now he’s president and he’s doing a fantastic job.” Nawrocki has suggested a new US military base in Poland will be called “Fort Trump”.
During its eight years in power – until 2023 - PiS appointed several judges to seats on the Tribunal already filled by the previous government.
In 2021, the European Union warned that PiS’ actions posed a “systemic risk to the rule of law in Poland” in undermining the Tribunal’s independence. The European Commission froze $137 billion in EU funding for Poland over concerns about the independence of Polish judges.
The PiS-appointed judges remained in place after Tusk was elected and have obstructed his efforts to nominate new judges. Nawrocki has refused to swear in three of six judges nominated by ‌parliament, ‌while Swieczkowski declined to seat the judges chosen by parliament.
Last week, the latest judge to be approved by parliament – Maciej Berek - was prevented from taking his seat amid scuffles outside the Tribunal in Warsaw.
On Saturday, riot police reinforced security measures around the court in central Warsaw.
Tusk, who has spent much of his time as Prime Minister trying to unstitch the PiS changes to the judiciary, said his government was seeking to restore the rule of law.
“This process is difficult, at times even painful, ‌and requires decisive action. There is no other way,” he said on X Saturday.
In a televised speech Tusk said that “shouting, lies, and brawling cannot be the source of law in Poland, and they never will be.”
He insisted the Tribunal “will function as it should. Also, independently of me and in line with the constitution.”
Analysts say the crisis deepened when parliament approved the nomination of Berek, a close ally of Tusk.
It “contradicts the government’s pledge to depoliticise the Tribunal,” wrote Alberto Allemano, a professor of law at the HEC Paris Business School.
“The Friday suspension of the Tribunal’s president and vice-president, ordered by one judge and accompanied by a police presence outside the building, is not in itself a “coup”: the stated aim is to restore a lawfully functioning court. But restoring the rule of law must itself be done lawfully,” Allemano wrote on X .
At the same time, “If the Polish government is trying to repair an institution captured under PiS, its opposition is striving to retain some control through illegal means,” he added.
The US ambassador to Poland Tom Rose warned on Friday night that “thousands gathering outside the tribunal make an already dangerous situation more combustible. The last thing Poland needs is a confrontation that spirals into something far worse.”
“I hope everyone involved—government officials, law enforcement, and demonstrators alike, to take a deep breath, and don’t take any action that could provoke violence or further escalation,” Rose said on X.
But it’s unclear how the standoff between Tusk and Nawrocki can be resolved. Neither seems ready to compromise at a time when Poland faces growing security threats – with the war across the border in Ukraine, and sabotage attacks inside Poland that Tusk has attributed to Russia.
Tusk said Saturday of his opponents that it was “no coincidence that they find support among pro-Russian forces around the world.”
Fresh elections are due next year, with Poland’s constitutional order and its political direction – towards or away from deeper integration with Europe – high on the agenda.

articles.title_orig: Ushakov: Putin Would Answer Phone Call From Zelensky
articles.title_zh: Ushakov: Putin Would Answer Phone Call From Zelensky
articles.content_orig:
Lavrov, who held a press conference on the sidelines of the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta, United States, indicated that his country would guarantee Zelenskyy’s safety and security—noting, however, that such guarantees could not be provided in Kyiv, the diplomatic ministry’s statement highlighted.
On September 12, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov described any potential meeting between Presidents Putin and Zelenskyy during the G20 summit in Miami as entirely “impossible.”
That same month, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced that Washington had invited Putin to the G20 summit.
In response, the Kremlin spokesperson stated that Russia appreciated the invitation and would consider it.
U.S. President Donald Trump had previously pointed to the need for a direct meeting between Putin and Zelenskyy to bring an end to the conflict in Ukraine, adding that he would “love” for Putin to attend the G20 summit.
The G20 consists of Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Germany, India, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, South Korea, Turkiye, the United Kingdom, the United States, and the European Union.

articles.title_orig: Fortnite Pirate Shop Explained: How to Unlock Access and Get Free Items
articles.title_zh: Fortnite Pirate Shop Explained: How to Unlock Access and Get Free Items
articles.content_orig:
Fortnite’s latest Treasure Hunters mini-season is out, and it brings a brand new feature called Pirate Shop, which allows players to get free skins and cosmetic items. Even though players can get free skins and items by completing quests through the latest Fortnite Treasure Hunters Battle Pass , the Pirate Shop lets them get their hands on some pricey loot for free. That said, here’s how you can unlock access to the Fortnite Pirate Shop and get free items.
The Pirate Shop is a brand-new token feature in Fortnite that allows players to purchase all the Item Shop cosmetics for free for a limited time after activation (pretty overpowered if you ask us). These tokens are hard to come by and can only be found in special containers around the Fortnite Treasure Hunters Crossbones Isle map .
However, you cannot use the Fortnite Pirate Shop token for real-money offers, gifting, pass levels, or sidekicks that you already own. So if you want to know how to get the Pirate Shop Access token in Fortnite, we’ve got you covered below.
To get a Pirate Shop Access token in Fortnite, you’ll need to find and open special containers called Treasure Hunt Chests in the new mini-season island. You’ll find these chests inside buildings of named POIs on the Crossbones Isle map in Fortnite.
As we mentioned earlier, Pirate Shop Access tokens are hard to come by; it’s purely up to luck and RNG if you can find one, since it’s one of the rarest items in Fortnite Treasure Hunters mini-season .
When you find the Pirate Shop Access token out of a Treasure Hunt Chest, the chest will glow golden and throw out some special loot items as well as a Pirate Shop Access token if you’re lucky enough.
But once you find any exclusive Treasure Chest item or the Pirate Access Token, your Fortnite friends who are in your party will also get it for absolutely free. This means even if one of your party members is lucky to find a Pirate Shop Access Token, everyone will be able to share their luck.
The Pirate Shop Access token is used to get all the paid skins and cosmetic items from the Fortnite Item Shop consecutively for 14 days, absolutely free. Think of these like Costume Coins in Marvel Rivals , but Fortnite’s version is a bit more overpowered.
Once you unlock a Pirate Shop Access token, you’ll be given a message when you return to the lobby that you can use the token once in 2026 and once in 2027. This means that winning this token gives you two activations. One you can activate from November 1 – December 15, 2026, and the second from January 1 – December 15, 2027.
To use it, head to the Fortnite Item Shop and click on the “Plunder the Item Shop” menu on the bottom right. It will present you with the activation menu for the Pirate Shop Access token in Fortnite. Click on “Activate Now,” and you’ll now be able to claim every single item inside the Fortnite Item Shop for absolutely free for the next 14 days, including the Luffy One Piece skin .
Furthermore, when you activate the token, you’ll have only 14 days to claim the entire Fortnite Item Shop for free without using any V-Bucks. Moreover, the Pirate Shop Access tokens are non-transferable, which means you cannot share them with a friend.
So, when will you activate and claim the entire Item Shop for free using the Fortnite Pirate Shop Access token? Let us know in the comments below!
Rishabh Sabarwal is a Gaming Editor at Beebom with over 7 years of experience covering the video game industry. He specializes in AAA releases and live-service games, and currently leads Beebom’s Gaming vertical, shaping editorial direction and daily coverage. When he’s not tracking the next big industry shift, Rishabh is busy cracking Wordles and curating puzzles for the Beebom Puzzle website.

articles.title_orig: Netanyahu’s Bid to Stay in Power Will Test His Political Savvy
articles.title_zh: Netanyahu’s Bid to Stay in Power Will Test His Political Savvy
articles.content_orig:
President Isaac Herzog on Sunday called on Israel's political leaders to accept the election results and demonstrate flexibility in coalition negotiations, warning against political entrenchment that could force the country into another election, ahead of consultations at the President’s Residence set to begin on Wednesday.
“The election results are an established fact – they are the reality. And now is the time to tell all the leaders: Stop climbing trees and position yourselves in front of this reality," Herzog said while speaking at the state memorial ceremony for Israel's first president, Chaim Weizmann.
Herzog made the remarks amid the political deadlock in which the election results showed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanayhu's bloc and the bloc seeking to oust the premier both fall short of the required 61-seat Knesset majority.
Netanyahu’s bloc maintained its lead, securing 53 seats in the next Knesset, while the opposition bloc won 48. Meanwhile, the Arab parties, Ra'am and the Joint List, won a record-breaking total of 19 seats combined.
The Joint List and Ra'am are expected to recommend Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot for prime minister during consultations with President Isaac Herzog, a senior Joint List official told Walla on Sunday.
Talks at the President's Residence will begin Wednesday, when Eisenkot is expected to be the first candidate to receive the mandate from the president, giving him 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, to form a coalition.
Along with the 48 seats won by the opposition bloc, the Arab parties' 19 recommendations would give Eisenkot 67 in total, prompting Herzog to grant him the mandate.
The Knesset is expected to be sworn in on November 10, regardless of any government or coalition talks.
By law, the president is required to consult the Knesset factions before deciding who receives the task of forming a government.
Herzog said that this week, at the President’s Residence, "we will try to put up ladders to allow the leaders to position themselves in front of this reality in a measured and careful manner."
Herzog said he would receive the official election results on Wednesday from Central Elections Committee chairman and Supreme Court Deputy President Justice Noam Sohlberg.
"Following that, I will begin consultations at the President's Residence. The President's Residence will be wide open to all factions and parties."
The president emphasized the importance of cooperation among party leaders, urging them to demonstrate a willingness to consider different proposals and reach agreements.
"I have already said that I hope the representatives will come with open minds, and I add that they should come with open hearts, to listen and share ideas and find creative solutions to prevent another election ," he said.
On Saturday, Eisenkot laid out four principles for joining his proposed coalition, saying that “any MK” willing to accept them could become a partner in forming the next government.
Eisenkot said he intended to establish the broadest possible Zionist, statesmanlike government, bringing together elected representatives who agree on Israel’s fundamental character, national service obligations, and the need to eliminate Hamas’s military and governing capabilities in the Gaza Strip.
Last week, Democrats party leader Yair Golan called on Wednesday for the opposition to form a coalition with the Arab parties.
Other heads of the opposition parties, Eisenkot, Naftali Bennett (B'Yachad), and Avigdor Liberman (Yisrael Beytenu), had drawn a red line to Arab parties being part of the government, saying they are not viable coalition partners after the October 7 massacre in 2023.
The political deadlock could ultimately lead to another election, although the parties may still reach an agreement through coalition negotiations. Other possible outcomes include a unity government among Netanyahu and members of Eisenkot’s bloc, or the formation of a minority government.
The Arab parties have expressed willingness to cooperate with the oppostion bloc to work toward replacing Netanyahu.
Meanwhile, opposition party leaders have also reportedly agreed that their first move after the new Knesset is sworn in on November 10 would be to oust Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana , a member of Netanyahu's Likud party.
The move would require a majority in a Knesset vote and could be achievable with the support of the Arab parties, bringing the potential backing to 67 seats.
Replacing Ohana would give the opposition bloc greater control over the parliamentary agenda, including votes, legislation, and committee appointments, even if Netanyahu remains in office as head of a caretaker government.
Jerusalem Post Staff contributed to this report.

articles.title_zh: At 97, China’s first female conductor still performs in public, wowing audiences
articles.content_orig:
Zheng notes that she never intentionally pursued a conducting career, choosing instead to ‘let everything happen naturally’
China’s first female conductor, Zheng Xiaoying, is 97 years old, but she continues to give outstanding performances to audiences.
In August, the nonagenarian conducted the Chinese-language version of the opera Carmen in Xiamen, in southeastern China’s Fujian province, where she lives. Tickets for the performance were like gold dust, and audiences marvelled, as always, at her elegant, expressive conducting.
Zheng has led a remarkable life. Born in Shanghai in 1929, she began studying piano at age six. During her university years, she switched to biology and medicine at the prestigious Peking Union Medical College Hospital. But at 19, she decided to flee to the liberated zone in search of “a new world she had never seen.”

articles.title_zh: 3 Hong Kong Chinese-language newspapers raise retail prices by HK$3
articles.content_orig:
Ming Pao, Hong Kong Economic Times and Hong Kong Economic Journal adjust prices by 20 to 25 per cent
Three Chinese-language newspapers in Hong Kong have raised their retail prices by HK$3 (40 US cents) this month, marking the first sector-wide adjustment in two years.
Ming Pao’s increase took effect on Sunday, raising its single-copy price from HK$12 to HK$15, up 25 per cent.
Two financial broadsheets will follow suit on Monday. The Hong Kong Economic Times (HKET) will raise its price from HK$12 to HK$15, while the Hong Kong Economic Journal (HKEJ) will increase its price by 20 per cent from HK$15 to HK$18.

articles.title_orig: Alibaba’s Qwen AI to power Apple Intelligence features in China
articles.title_zh: Alibaba’s Qwen AI to power Apple Intelligence features in China
articles.content_orig:
Alibaba’s flagship AI model Qwen will be integrated into Apple Intelligence, after years of speculation and regulatory uncertainty
Apple’s long-awaited artificial intelligence features will be officially launched in China in December, ending two years of regulatory uncertainty as the US tech giant seeks to bring advanced technologies to its second-largest market with the help of Alibaba Group Holding.
The first batch of Apple Intelligence services will roll out to Chinese iPhone users alongside the iOS 27.3 update in December, following an open beta test with developers starting November 4, the US company said in a statement on Saturday.
The initial roll-out will include around 18 new features provided by Apple Intelligence, including writing tools for summarising and proofreading, live translation for phone calls and messages, as well as visual intelligence via camera controls, according to the statement.

articles.title_orig: Rioters smash, loot storefronts amid cost of living protests in Germany
articles.title_zh: Rioters smash, loot storefronts amid cost of living protests in Germany
articles.content_orig:
Masked rioters smashed storefronts and looted goods late Saturday in Frankfurt, Germany amid a protest against the rising cost of living.
The largely peaceful demonstrations were led by a youth initiative called "Gen Z regelt" - roughly translated to "Gen Z's got this" - rallied in more than 30 cities "for education, health, climate protection and an affordable life," and against any return of military conscription. Organizers said that tens of thousands participated in the protests across the country, but official figures weren't immediately available.
Tensions peaked in the evening as some groups of protesters refused to disperse, sparking clashes and violence in major cities including Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg.
in Frankfurt's financial hub, masked protesters hurled stones, fireworks and pepper bombs, according to police.
Authorities also said looters stole weapons from a gun store, which were later retrieved. Some rioters also threw Molotov cocktails at police after pummeling them with stones and bottles earlier in the day, Frankfurt police said on X.
In the northern city of Hamburg, some protesters also shot pyrotechnics toward police and burned down barricades. Police responded by using water cannons and tear gas to disperse the crowds.
Earlier in the day, demonstrations had been largely peaceful. In Berlin, young protesters gathered at Brandenburg Gate on Saturday afternoon, demanding more investments in education and housing.
"We call for more money to be invested in social services and education, as well as in climate protection - in short, in our future - because we are the ones who will be affected by this the longest and who will have to live with it," high school student Lara Breitenbach said.
Janelle Schulz, another high school student from Berlin, also said that the authorities had to invest more money in education.
"At my school, the ceiling is collapsing because of water damage, nothing is being done about it, we have a shortage of teachers, the toilets are broken," she said.
AFP contributed to this report.

Like other middle powers, the Central Asian nation is striving to build a new AI economy while bridging a widening US-China tech divide
Driving along the wide boulevards of Astana during a recent trip to the Kazakh capital, signs of China’s growing commercial footprint were everywhere.
Chinese cars were becoming a common sight on the streets here, as brands from BYD to Changan made aggressive inroads in a market once dominated by South Korea’s Hyundai and Kia, said the driver who picked me up from the airport in a gleaming Changan electric vehicle.
But it was not the rise of Chinese tech that had brought me to this energy-rich pocket of Central Asia; it was an American giant.

articles.title_orig: Military briefing: what would another US-Iran conflict look like?
articles.title_zh: Military briefing: what would another US-Iran conflict look like?
articles.content_orig:
Israel could unleash a devastating surprise attack targeting Iran's top military leaders if war resumes after Tuesday's midterm elections, potentially employing tactics similar to its sophisticated 2024 operation that crippled Hezbollah, the New York Post reported Saturday.
The USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier is reportedly heading to the Middle East to join the USS George Washington and USS George W. Bush as President Donald Trump weighs renewed military action against Tehran.
Trump told Kansas City radio station KCMO Friday that the conflict is "going to get wrapped up soon," although he did not elaborate.
Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., predicted military action could come immediately after the elections.
"I'm going to guess about a day or three after this election, I would not want to be anywhere close to Iran," Marshall said Thursday.
Former Mossad Deputy Head of Global Operations Oded Ailam told the outlet that Israel could execute another operation resembling its extraordinary September 2024 pager attack against Hezbollah, this time targeting four Iranian military hard-liners believed to exercise effective control over the regime.
"This is the bread and butter of Israeli strategy, is surprise twists and turns, unexpected moves and I'm absolutely certain that Israel has cards in the sleeve that will be used," Ailam said.
The 2024 operation was among the most creative, planned and devastating intelligence attacks in modern warfare.
On Sept. 17-18, thousands of explosive-rigged pagers and walkie-talkies used by Hezbollah operatives detonated across Lebanon and Syria, killing dozens, injuring thousands and severely disrupting the Iranian-backed terrorist organization's communications.
The meticulously coordinated attack required years of planning, sophisticated intelligence gathering, and infiltration of Hezbollah's communications supply chain, demonstrating Israel's extraordinary ability to identify, penetrate, and strike its enemies from within.
That precedent raises the possibility that Israeli intelligence already knows the identities, movements, and vulnerabilities of Iran's military leadership and has spent years preparing similarly unexpected operations.
According to Ailam, Iran's real power rests with four military figures: Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander Ahmad Vahidi, Basij commander Hossein Taeb, armed forces chief Ali Abdollahi and Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei.
"The president and foreign minister can't make decisions. [The military junta] hides behind Mojtaba, but he's not in charge; he's a complete puppet," Ailam said, referring to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei.
"Israel will use its imagination, its intelligence and the ability of the Israelis to surprise and turn the table in ways you can not anticipate," he added.
Ailam said the Iranian leadership is increasingly divided over negotiations with Washington, with military hard-liners repeatedly undermining diplomatic efforts.
"They're not on the same page themselves, we see a lot of friction within the regime, different approaches, agreeing then reneging," he said.
Retired U.S. Gen. Jack Keane advocated strikes against Iran's leadership, nuclear facilities, energy infrastructure and missile and drone production capabilities.
"The intelligence we have now as a result of six months of collection during the on-again, off-again ceasefire is significant," Keane said.
Ailam suggested that another Israeli intelligence operation could inflict psychological damage exceeding that of a conventional military invasion.
"The effect is enormous, especially on the psychology of the enemy. Imagine after the attack there's a conversation somewhere in a bunker with the top echelons of Iran and everybody's looking to the left and to the right and thinking the guy next to him is a spy," he said.
However, analysts warned that renewed attacks could provoke devastating Iranian retaliation.
"[The regime's] interest is survival; they'll fight harder," said Behnam Ben Taleblu, senior director of the Iran Program at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies.
Former IDF Maj. Gen. Yaakov Amidror warned that Iranian strikes against Gulf energy infrastructure could trigger an overwhelming Israeli response.
"If the Iranian retaliation will be to destroy or try to destroy energy facilities in the Gulf countries, that would be a good excuse for Israel to destroy the whole energy infrastructure in Iran," Amidror said.
"This is something that cannot be rebuilt in a few years, this will send Iran back 50 years," he added.
Meanwhile, Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., pushed back against the Trump administration's reported military planning.
"Their plan is insane. It will lead to devastating escalation and the likely destruction of our commitment to the rule of law," Murphy said Thursday.
"The plan that they have developed will lead in my view to a prolongment and an escalation of this war that in my view will be devastating for our security interests," he added.
Despite any speculation about a leadership strike, Amidror emphasized that Israel's overriding military priority remains eliminating Iran's nuclear weapons potential and ballistic missile capabilities.

articles.title_orig: Reeves says UK's future should be inside the EU
articles.title_zh: Reeves says UK's future should be inside the EU
articles.content_orig:
Former Chancellor Rachel Reeves has argued the UK's future should be inside the EU, and that Brexit has made the country "poorer, weaker and less secure".
In her first major intervention since leaving the Treasury, Reeves said she welcomed debate around the UK's relationship with Europe.
At the last election, Labour's manifesto said a Labour government would stay outside the EU and make Brexit work.
But Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said there needs to be an honest discussion about what the future relationship looks like.
The Conservatives have said there is no desire to rerun the Brexit debate and Reform UK's Nigel Farage has said there is no mandate to pursue closer EU ties.
Labour's 2024 election manifesto ruled out a return of free movement, single market membership or a customs union.
Burnham has said that any changes would require a mandate at a general election, which is next due by 2029.
In the Sunday Times , Reeves wrote: "No-one in the Treasury ever doubted where my instincts were. I do believe Britain's future lies in the European Union."
She said supporters of rejoining the EU had to "make the argument, demonstrate tangible benefits and to get the next steps right".
Reeves added that at the forthcoming UK-EU summit, she hoped for confirmation of the youth mobility scheme she has been pushing for since she was in office.
She also said she was hoping for "progress towards entry" into the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) scheme.
Announced last March, SAFE is part of an EU-wide effort to rearm after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
A defence pact agreed with the EU last May paved the way for UK-based defence companies to be part of projects funded by SAFE.
In her piece for the Sunday Times, Reeves also sought to defend her record in office.
She wrote about the need for governments to be "braver" in building big infrastructure projects and "clear eyed" about the risks and benefits AI would drive in advanced economies.

articles.title_orig: Thousands rally in Israel urging ‘Jewish-Arab’ coalition to oust Netanyahu
articles.title_zh: Thousands rally in Israel urging ‘Jewish-Arab’ coalition to oust Netanyahu
articles.content_orig:
Thousands of people have rallied in Tel Aviv to urge the Israeli opposition to make a deal with Arab parties to remove Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Protesters at Saturday’s rally told the AFP news agency this may be the “last chance for real change” and that Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, is a “great manipulator”.
Main opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has previously ruled out forming a coalition with Israel’s Arab parties, but a deadlock in Tuesday’s elections means siding with the parties could help him form a government.
“People really want this vote for change to work out, and they believe that… Gadi Eisenkot and other leaders of the Jewish-Israeli parties need to listen to their voice,” Al Jazeera correspondent Nour Odeh said from Ramallah on Saturday.
Counter-protesters also showed up to Saturday’s demonstrations, with Netanyahu supporters seen shouting their own demands that “Israel should not have a government with so-called terrorists”, Odeh said.
Netanyahu’s bloc won 53 seats in Tuesday’s elections, while Eisenkot’s won 48, meaning neither side can form a government in Israel’s 120-seat parliament alone.
Israel’s three Arab-led parties won 19 seats, having made significant gains in Tuesday’s election.
Nearly 840,000 people voted for Ra’am and the Joint List, a coalition of three Arab-led parties, a 64 percent increase from the last elections in 2022, according to the Central Election Committee.
The Arab electoral success means a coalition with Eisenkot would provide a comfortable majority of 67. However, for many in Israel, the idea of siding with Arabs is politically unpalatable.
Netanyahu has accused Palestinian-Israeli parties of “stealing” the polls and accepting funding from Qatar to do it. Qatar has rejected the allegations , calling it a disinformation campaign.
Odeh said that Israeli right-wing circles have described “the historic turnout of Palestinian Israelis as electoral terrorism, equating it to the October 7th attack”, when Hamas-led fighters stormed southern Israel, killing more than 1,200 people and taking hundreds captive.
“Palestinian-Israeli votes and voices” are under attack because they have a “prominent position” in deciding whether Eisenkot can form a government, she added.

articles.title_orig: How the downfall of Serbia's Vučiċ mirrored that of Hungary's Orbán
articles.title_zh: How the downfall of Serbia's Vučiċ mirrored that of Hungary's Orbán
articles.content_orig:
When they met in northern Serbia last November, Serbian President Aleksandar Vučiċ and Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán could hardly have guessed they would both be out of power within a year.
Both were ousted by popular movements - Orbán fell first, in April, defeated by Péter Magyar's Tisza party. Then last Sunday a student movement less than two years old won Serbia's parliamentary elections by a landslide.
The Tisza party in Hungary and the Student List in Serbia look very different - Tisza is centred on the personality and energy of its leader, while the students in Serbia insist they have no leadership.
But the huge turnout - 79% in Hungary and 69% in Serbia, was driven by tech-savvy young people in both countries. They used AI tools to crunch numbers, identify threats to the vote, and mobilise tens of thousands of election monitors to prevent intimidation and electoral fraud by the governing parties.
Mobilisation of voters, and the role of election monitors, played a big role in the opposition victory in both countries.
Last weekend, the DE civic action group in Hungary sent 70 election monitors to Serbia, to work with students' movement representatives, visiting polling stations in the northern Serbian province of Vojvodina.
During the summer, even before the election was called, they held workshops to share their experience and methods from the Hungarian election with the Serbian students.
A key technique was to identify "infected" polling districts in advance - places where the surprisingly high number of votes for the governing party at previous elections suggested that voter intimidation or "chain voting" techniques were used.
"From around 16:00 on election day, we noticed groups of masked hooligans - Vučiċ supporters - gathering near voting stations," Péter Klemm, a student activist from Subotica, told the BBC. "So we sent mobile teams, and started filming everything."
Combined with the "stationary" monitors already in place, 20 to 30 volunteers at each threatened polling station acted as a strong deterrent, he believes, and prevented intimidation or fraud.
Orbán in Hungary, Vučiċ in Serbia, both looked invincible. Both were powerful leaders, in office for 16 and 14 years, who had taken over state institutions and established business empires overlapping the two countries.
Orban chose cheese, Vučiċ meat, when they sat down to a quick lunch of traditional burek pastries at a small, popular town centre bakery in Subotica almost a year ago.
They continued to a local winery, to talk about oil and other business deals - the planned Hungarian purchase of Serbia's Nis oil refinery. The two nationalist leaders found much in common, in business and politics, not least their friendship with Vladimir Putin in Russia and Chinese President Xi Jinping, and their strong support for Milorad Dodik, the separatist leader of the Bosnian Serbs.
A high-speed railway between Belgrade and Budapest is being built with Chinese finance and know-how.
The parallels between the fall from power of the two men are extraordinary. Aleksandar Vučiċ admitted defeat at exactly 21:30 on Sunday evening, just as Viktor Orbán did on 12 April. Few observers expected either leader to concede peacefully.
There has been speculation this week that Vučiċ spoke to Orbán twice on Sunday night to ask his advice - once before he conceded, and again at 23:15. And that Orbán convinced his Serbian ally not to use force.
Vučiċ denies that he spoke to Orbán before he made his announcement, but acknowledges the later conversation. Viktor Orbán, contacted by the BBC, declined to comment.
An hour before polls closed in Serbia, masked and hooded vigilantes took up position in central Belgrade. During voting, similar groups were photographed at many polling stations, and blocked by election monitors.
There is another strange numerical similarity. The Student List will have 140 seats in the 250-seat Serbian parliament, the same number Péter Magyar's Tisza party won in the 199-seat Hungarian parliament.
Magyar was the only European leader to ring the students directly to congratulate them that evening - and probably the only one who had their number.
"It is always good to hear that the story of Tisza could provide an inspiration for other nations," the Hungarian prime minister told the BBC.
"The result of the Hungarian election clearly showed us that what we are doing here is right," the head of the Student List, Ilija Srdanoviċ, said on the eve of the vote.
Srdanoviċ was one of those Péter Magyar spoke to that Sunday evening.
Orbán, 63, and Vučiċ, 56, may now both face prosecution for corruption and abuse of power.
The judicial machinery in both countries is similar. Serbia's special prosecution service for organised crime, JTOK, and Hungary's brand new special prosecutors, known as NVVH, have similar powers. They could prove useful to each other.
Hungarian companies close to Orbán were also involved in the Novi Sad railway station construction project. The collapse of the station's canopy on 1 November 2024 - blamed on corruption, as well as negligence - killed 16 people, and acted as the catalyst for the Serbian student movement.
"There was a perception in Europe that the longer the Orbán and Vučiċ regimes stayed in office, the stronger they got," Áron Timar, founder of the DE civic action group in Hungary told the BBC.
"In fact they got weaker. And once society found its voice and rose up, there was no way of stopping it."

articles.title_orig: Rahul Gandhi: India's opposition rallies against voter roll revision exercise
articles.title_zh: Rahul Gandhi: India's opposition rallies against voter roll revision exercise
articles.content_orig:
Tens of thousands of people have gathered in India's capital Delhi for a major opposition rally demanding the resignation of the country's chief election commissioner over a controversial revision of voter lists.
The rally, organised by the opposition INDIA bloc and led by Rahul Gandhi's Congress party, has brought together some of India's most prominent politicians at Ramlila Maidan, a sprawling ground in central Delhi.
They arrived at the venue on Sunday after travelling in jeeps through crowds of cheering supporters.
Among those attending were Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, as well as Mamata Banerjee, Akhilesh Yadav and Tejashwi Yadav.
The rally comes after weeks of opposition protests over a voter-list revision exercise that has removed 130 million names from draft electoral rolls.
Opposition parties accuse chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of using the exercise to manipulate elections. Both the BJP and the Election Commission deny the allegations.
Protesters chanted "Save the vote, save the country" and "Vote thief, give up power", while others sang and danced to patriotic Bollywood songs. Thousands of police and paramilitary personnel were deployed around the venue, with barricades and traffic restrictions in place.
The Gen Z-led pressure group Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has also pledged support, though its leaders have yet to be seen at the event.
Among those protesting on Sunday was Isha, a development sector professional from Delhi, who said she feared Indian democracy was under threat.
"We don't even know if this is a people's mandate or a stolen mandate," she told the BBC.
Deepro Guha, a lawyer from Delhi, said he was concerned about the way the revision had been carried out.
"It's important because voting is the basis of democracy. If people's names are removed without any explanation, there is a problem," he said.
The exercise, known as the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), is intended to remove people who have died, moved away from their registered addresses or are otherwise ineligible to vote, according to the ECI.
But the opposition alleges that eligible voters are being deliberately removed to benefit the governing BJP.
The controversy intensified in September after The Indian Express newspaper reported that Kumar had made key decisions relating to the exercise despite objections from the two other election commissioners on more than a dozen occasions.
The Election Commission said differences of opinion were normal in any institution and did not affect its functioning.
Ahead of the event, Gandhi described the opposition's campaign as a fight against "the demolition of Indian democracy" and said millions of people were being disenfranchised.
On Saturday, leaders of the INDIA bloc also staged a symbolic impeachment of Kumar at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence in Delhi. The INDIA bloc - short for Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance - is a group of opposition parties formed in 2023 to take on the governing BJP-led National Democratic Alliance.
The mock parliamentary session, presided over by former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar, saw leaders accuse the election chief of "conspiring to steal elections" and deliberately removing 130 million voters from electoral rolls.
The proceedings were purely symbolic and had no legal standing. Under Indian law, the chief election commissioner can only be removed through a formal parliamentary process.
Modi has not directly commented on the mock impeachment, but at public rallies on Friday and Saturday he accused opposition parties of trying to create chaos and undermining the dignity of the constitution.
Delhi police have given permission to hold Sunday's rally, but it comes with several conditions. Media reports say the rally must end by 5pm, CCTV cameras must be installed at the venue and no marches will be allowed outside the designated protest site.
The rally has also divided opinion among traders in Chandni Chowk, one of Delhi's oldest and busiest markets, located less than a kilometre from Ramlila Maidan.
Earlier this week, a group of traders said the protest could hurt business during the festive season, coming just a week before Diwali.
But a rival group of traders said they supported Gandhi's rally and criticised the BJP for taking out a march through the market on Thursday, saying that disrupted the festive season more.
Ahead of the event, Gandhi had appealed to people to turn up in large numbers. "Don't worry about the police, don't worry about lathis [batons] - the BJP will not have the guts to try any of their antics," he wrote on X.
His comments come amid growing concerns about the policing of recent protests in the capital.
On 10 October, thousands of security personnel were deployed and large parts of the city were shut down to thwart protests called by the CJP against CEC Gyanesh Kumar.
All of the top CJP leaders were detained and many demonstrators were beaten and dragged through the streets to break up their protests. BBC reporters covering demonstrations saw police dragging away protesters and using batons on some of them.
Last month, Gandhi led tens of thousands of protesters in a march from Connaught Place in central Delhi to the Supreme Court, seeking the CEC's resignation.
"The march was just the trailer," a party leader told the BBC, adding that "Sunday's rally will be several times bigger than that".

articles.title_orig: Southeast Asia’s EV boom sidelines local car parts suppliers
articles.title_zh: Southeast Asia’s EV boom sidelines local car parts suppliers
articles.content_orig:
Suppliers in Indonesia, Thailand and Malaysia grapple with falling demand, as Chinese carmakers favour their own networks
Local manufacturers across Indonesia, Thailand and Malaysia are facing a double squeeze: demand is weakening for parts used in petrol and diesel cars, collectively known as internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles, while steep barriers to entry also keep them out of EV supply chains.
Analysts say repair and servicing work plus hybrids, which pair a petrol engine with an electric motor, could offer a lifeline, but without stronger government support and better access to Chinese manufacturers, the EV transition threatens to hollow out the region’s established supply base.
Chinese EV investments have so far generated minimal business for established local component makers, according to Indonesian economist Bhima Yudhistira Adhinegara.

articles.title_orig: A third weekend of protests in France as youth-led rallies sweep Europe
articles.title_zh: A third weekend of protests in France as youth-led rallies sweep Europe
articles.content_orig:
Massive protests were sweeping Europe on Saturday as part of demonstrations driven by the cost of living and deficient public services, with police bracing for potential violence after recent looting and riots.
Germany, France, Spain and Italy are among the nations where demonstrations were being held on Halloween following a recent wave of Gen Z-led marches across the continent.
French officials said they would deploy 70,000 police on Saturday following some of the worst rioting in decades , which erupted in cities across the country after student protests about the state of education evolved into wider demonstrations about the cost of living and social security.
As the demonstrations began Saturday afternoon in Paris, protesters were pictured holding a banner that read: “We do not need tear gas for our future to be blurry.”
Videos vetted by NBC News show large crowds and fires burning in Marseille.
Some 320,000 people demonstrated across France on Saturday, including 70,000 in Paris, according to the French Interior Ministry. Authorities reported more than 560 arrests nationwide by Saturday night.
While the protests have been largely peaceful, police arrested 1,300 people last week after an estimated 410,000 took to the streets in cities across the country. Stores, public buildings and businesses have also been damaged since the protests erupted last month.
“Everyone is ​on deck to ensure an extremely firm response to any trouble,” Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said at a news conference earlier this week as he set out security arrangements, adding there was “a very high ⁠risk” of unrest.
Measures introduced last week to protect shops would be reinforced, he said, and demonstrations would not be permitted “in city centers, where there is a risk of public disorder.”
The U.S. Embassy in France advised travelers to avoid areas ​where demonstrations or large gatherings are planned.
The protests in France began after Prime Minister Emmanuel Macron launched budget talks for 2027. Students in the country, angry over a declining education system and the high cost of living, then took to the streets.
They were later joined by unions and the Yellow Vests, a grassroots movement that emerged in 2018 as a revolt against fuel taxes.
Those demonstrations appear to have inspired similar protests across the continent, with protests erupting in Belgium, Spain, Italy and elsewhere.
In Germany there were demonstrations organized by the campaign group Gen Z regelt (Gen Z takes charge) in more than 30 cities Saturday, including the capital Berlin and the financial hub Frankfurt.
The groups demand spending on schools, climate protection and housing, and are against plans to return to mandatory military service.
“We all have those images from France in our minds — looting, burning houses, burning police vehicles, and attacks on police officers,” said Roman Poseck, interior minister for the state of Hesse, whose capital is Frankfurt.
Protesters gathered in front of Berlin’s Brandenburg Gate, as police said an additional 1,500 officers would be deployed throughout the city.
While most people rallied peacefully, some protests turned violent on Saturday night.
In downtown Frankfurt, some rioters smashed several storefronts and stole goods from inside. They also stole weapons from a gun store, which police were able to retrieve later. Some rioters also threw Molotov cocktails at police after pummeling them with stones and bottles earlier in the day, Frankfurt police said on X.
Elsewhere in Europe, a huge encampment of tents has occupied a square in Madrid since late last month, and thousands of people in Portugal have taken to the streets in the city of Lisbon. Tear gas and water cannons were also used on black-clad protesters in Brussels.
In the United Kingdom, hundreds of demonstrators are expected to gather outside the U.S. Embassy in London on Saturday and risk arrest in support of Palestine Action, a protest group banned by the British government.
In Serbia, student-led activism also helped unseat the country’s long-time leader at the ballot box.
In Italy , Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s far-right government also said it would deploy 500 army troops alongside the police in Milan until the end of the year after groups of masked protesters looted stores in the fashion capital and elsewhere and threw projectiles at police earlier this month.
Tens of thousands of people again took to the streets of Rome on Friday and other cities and towns across the country.
The demonstrations were largely peaceful, but an NBC News crew saw police use a water cannon on protesters and groups of police charging to disperse protesters.
Italian police were out in force with riot brigades, drones and helicopters visible in the skies above the capital.
“We have been completely screwed by the fact that the wages do not keep up on inflation and the wages in general do not keep up with the cost of living,” said Luca, a 20-year-old medical student who asked to have his last name withheld out of fear of repercussions from law enforcement.
Freddie Clayton is a freelance journalist based in London.

articles.title_orig: Eisenkot vows to swiftly utilize Knesset majority ‘against Oct. 7 government’
articles.title_zh: Eisenkot vows to swiftly utilize Knesset majority ‘against Oct. 7 government’
articles.content_orig:
Yashar chairman Gadi Eisenkot laid out four principles for joining his proposed coalition on Saturday, saying that “any MK” willing to accept them could become a partner in forming the next government.
Election Day results saw Yashar win 21 seats in the Knesset, with the Eisenkot bloc at 48 total; the Likud won 27 seats, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc at 53 overall; and the Arab parties won 19 seats.
After the completion of the vote count, Eisenkot said he intended to establish the broadest possible Zionist, statesmanlike government, bringing together elected representatives who agree on Israel’s fundamental character, national service obligations, and the need to eliminate Hamas’s military and governing capabilities in the Gaza Strip.
“Any MK willing to sign on to these principles is a potential partner in establishing a new government that will be good for Israel,” Eisenkot said. “The door to the government we establish will be open to any elected official who accepts these principles and is prepared to rise to the occasion.”
Eisenkot’s conditions for any prospective coalition partner are: The recognition of Israel as a Jewish, democratic, liberal, and egalitarian state; a commitment to the values of the Declaration of Independence; mandatory military, national, or civilian service for all Israeli citizens; and recognition of Hamas as a terrorist organization and acknowledgment of the obligation to destroy its military and governing power in the Gaza Strip.
Eisenkot said the principles would serve as the foundation for a broad government based on national consensus, rather than one seeking to impose the will of one political camp on another.
This latest development came amid a demonstration in Tel Aviv calling for a government of Arab and Jewish parties.
During the election campaign, Eisenkot pledged to establish a government capable of healing divisions and fundamentally changing Israel’s direction.
“I promised to reconnect Israel and put an end to the culture of lies led by Netanyahu that has torn us apart from within,” Eisenkot said. “I promised that under my leadership, one side would not defeat the other, and that the era of ‘us’ and ‘them’ was over.”
He said he would continue pursuing those commitments in the coming weeks while coordinating with his political partners to broaden the potential coalition.
“Based on these principles, I intend to establish the broadest possible Zionist, statesmanlike government,” Eisenkot said, adding that he aimed to fulfill the voters’ wishes and immediately improve Israel’s domestic and international standing.
Meanwhile, Yisrael Beytenu leader Avigdor Liberman denied reports that he was interested in becoming Knesset speaker in a post on X/Twitter on Saturday.
“The wicked never rest. I have received several inquiries regarding demands for the position of Knesset speaker. I have no desire and no intention of becoming Knesset speaker,” he wrote.

articles.title_orig: Air Astana and China Southern Airlines Sign Joint Venture Amid 52% Flight Growth
articles.title_zh: Air Astana and China Southern Airlines Sign Joint Venture Amid 52% Flight Growth
articles.content_orig:
A global review of commercial flight
Air Astana (KC) and China Southern Airlines (CZ) announced on October 30, 2026, that they had signed a joint venture (JV) agreement to strengthen air connectivity between Kazakhstan and China. The agreement marks the first airline joint venture between the countries.
Building on their existing codeshare partnership, the airlines will coordinate schedules, expand codeshare services and undertake joint marketing initiatives.
“The number of flights between our countries has increased by 52 per cent compared with the same period in 2025 (117 scheduled flights per week across 21 routes). Since the start of 2026, more than one million passengers have been carried. The Ministry plans to further expand the route network with China, increasing it to 30 destinations,” said Talgat Lastaev, Deputy Minister of Transport of the Republic of Kazakhstan.
“China is a strategically important market for Air Astana, and Kazakhstan is well positioned as a gateway connecting Europe and Asia. Our joint venture with China Southern Airlines represents an important step in developing this role and deepening our commercial relationship with one of China’s leading carriers. By combining our complementary networks and aligning key aspects of our commercial offering, we aim to provide passengers with greater choice, more convenient connections and more consistent conditions and rules across both airlines. At the same time, closer cooperation will enable us to respond more effectively to passenger demand and support the continued growth of air travel between Kazakhstan and China,” said Richard Ledger, VP, Partnerships and Alliances of Air Astana.
Zeng Yongchao, executive vice president of China Southern Airlines, stated: "China and Kazakhstan are important partners under the Belt and Road framework. This joint venture is a substantive achievement in aviation connectivity between the two countries and reflects our shared aspiration for a prosperous regional market. For both airlines, this is a strategic choice that leverages our respective strengths and shares resources. For passengers, the most tangible benefit is greater convenience: more flight options, smoother transfer procedures, and a more seamless travel experience. We hope every passenger journeying along the Belt and Road's air routes will feel the difference this cooperation brings."
On Thursday, October 29, Air Astana announced it had begun equipping its Airbus A321LR fleet with high-speed satellite Wi-Fi . The project was launched in partnership with SES, a global satellite communications provider, and the airline is installing the equipment at its own technical facility.
The first Airbus A321LR equipped with high-speed satellite Wi-Fi operated its first internet-connected flight on October 29 on the Almaty–Tashkent route.

articles.title_orig: London police arrest 139 people outside US Embassy for supporting banned pro-Palestinian group
articles.title_zh: London police arrest 139 people outside US Embassy for supporting banned pro-Palestinian group
articles.content_orig:
Met alleges demonstrators ‘meeting to purposefully commit a crime’ in largest such gathering under Burnham
Almost 140 people have been arrested at the largest mass demonstrations under Andy Burnham’s premiership opposing the proscription of Palestine Action.
Hundreds of people gathered outside the US embassy in Battersea, south London, holding signs that read: “I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action.” Demonstrators also held a vigil in support of the group outside the US consulate in Edinburgh.
Before the London gathering, the Metropolitan police warned those taking part “that they face arrest as part of a robust policing operation” and that anyone “playing a key role in organising the event, giving instructions to others and/or providing logistical support” would probably be committing an offence.
In a statement on X, the Metropolitan police said: “139 people have now been arrested. Officers remain on scene and are continuing to make arrests.”
Commander Adam Slonecki, who is leading the policing operation, said: “All those intending on coming to this event know that supporting a proscribed organisation is unlawful – they are essentially meeting to purposefully commit a crime.
Defend Our Juries, the group behind the demonstrations, said the Met was “terrified of facilitating US embarrassment” and estimated that “around 400 people” gathered to take part.
More than 4,000 arrests have been made for supporting Palestine Action since the ban came into effect, Defend Our Juries said, representing the vast majority of terror arrests since last July.
Among those sitting outside the US embassy, holding a sign that appeared to express support for Palestine Action, was Sue Morhall. “The USA is complicit in most of the wars that are going on. I just feel the leaders of this world, including Trump, need to know that people are so against what’s happening in Gaza,” said the 79-year-old retiree.
Morhall believes there is a chance Burnham could rescind the proscription. “I think it’s early days. I’m hopeful, though pigs might fly,” she said. “I think he’s going to perhaps wait until the midterm elections in America. It’s a terrible shame that people who are trying to stop a genocide are being arrested.”
She has been arrested “five or six” times at previous demonstrations and feels “OK” about being hauled into a police van again. “It’s the principle, and this is one that I feel very strongly about,” she said.
The Rev Bill White, 72, who also held a sign that read: “I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action,” said: “I’m appalled that Britain is helping facilitate the genocide that is happening in Palestine. We supply weapons that are being used on Palestinians.”
He said he had “hoped for better” from Burnham and resigned from the Labour party after Palestine Action was proscribed as a terrorist group.
As a faith leader, he said there was “no choice” other than to take part in the demonstration. “This is the right thing to do. There’s a bad law and it is wrong to criminalise people that are trying to prevent genocide,” he said. “How can I not be here?”
A Defend Our Juries spokesperson said: “The Met police overzealous response outside the US embassy today only serves to further expose how far authorities in the UK will go to appease American interests. Israel’s war crimes that have caused death and injury to thousands could not happen without the US’s approval.”
The protests come before an appeal at the UK supreme court against Palestine Action’s designation as a terror group on 4 November.
Last month, more than 160 people were arrested or reported for summons at a similar demonstration in support of Palestine Action staged outside the Labour party conference in Liverpool.
The new government has come under pressure to rescind the ban, though Shabana Mahmood, who has stood firm in favour of the group’s proscription, remained in post as home secretary.
The journalist and author Sarah Helm, the wife of the prime minister’s national security adviser, Jonathan Powell, was accused of supporting Palestine Action after posting on X : “God help us authors who support Palestine and Palestine Action.” Her post came in response to news that the Irish author Sally Rooney can no longer sell her books in the UK because of her support for the group.
During the Labour party conference, two activists confronted the foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, during a meal at Pizza Express in the city centre where he was challenged about the arrests. Video of the incident showed one of the protesters urging Miliband to declare a genocide in Gaza and de-proscribe Palestine Action.
Miliband said he was happy to discuss the issue but at another time, before the protesters were ushered out.
One woman, who held a sign that, bar swapping the word “authors” to “retirees”, replicated the X post by Sarah Helm, was among those arrested in London, despite the Met ultimately assessing that Helm’s post “did not meet the criminal threshold”.
